steps.action: Grow Cor3-1 neural stem cells in Complete media containing DMEM/HAM’S-F12, 1.45% Glucose, 1× MEM-NEAA, 100 units/ml penicillin, 100 μg/ml streptomycin, 0.16% BSA, 0.1 mM β-Mercapto-ethanol, 1% B-27 supplement, and 0.5% N2 supplement.
Before changing the medium or passaging, add 10 ng/ml mouse EGF, 10 ng/ml human FGF, and 1 μg/ml Laminin to the Complete media.
For neuronal differentiation, 24 hours after seeding, transfer cells to priming medium Euromed-N supplemented with 1% B-27 without vitamin A, 0.5% N2, and 10 ng/ml human FGF for 3 days.

Transfer cells to differentiation medium with a 1:3 ratio DMEM/HAM’S-F12:Neurobasal supplemented with 1% B-27 without vitamin A, 0.5% N2, 10 ng/ml human FGF, 20 ng/ml BDNF, and 1μg/ml Laminin for 3 days.
Change the medium every 3 days, reducing the FGF concentration by half each time until it reaches zero, while maintaining a constant concentration of BDNF at 30 ng/ml.
For Huwe1 knock-out, transduce Floxed-Huwe1-RYFP neural stem cells with adenovirus CMV-CRE at a MOI of 100 or use empty adenovirus (CMV-null) as a control.
Maintain P19 cells in MEM-α supplemented with 10% FBS, 100 units/ml penicillin, and 100 μg/ml streptomycin.

For differentiation of P19 cells, transfer them into Neurobasal medium supplemented with penicillin/streptomycin, 1% B-27 without vitamin A, 1× GlutaMAX, and 1μg/ml Laminin, changing the medium every 24 hours if required.
Transfect P19 cells at 80% confluence with Lipofectamine 2000 in proliferation medium following the manufacturer’s instructions with a 1:2 ratio of DNA:Lipofectamine.
Extract total RNA from cells using the RNeasy kit.
Synthesise template cDNAs using the QuantiTect Reverse Transcription Kit.
Perform qRT-PCR using QuantiFast SYBR Green Master Mix in a Lightcycler 480 PCR system with EiF1α as the housekeeping gene.
Carry out thermal cycling for qRT-PCR at 95°C for 5 mins, followed by 40 cycles of 95°C for 10 seconds, 60°C for 10 seconds, and 72°C for 30 seconds.
Perform western blotting from total cell lysates or fractionated lysates using RIPA buffer with protease inhibitor cocktail.
Determine protein concentration using BCA protein assay kit.
Carry out SDS-PAGE electrophoresis in 10% pre-cast polyacrylamide gels in MOPS buffer.
Transfer proteins onto nitrocellulose and block membranes with 10% non-fat milk in TBS-0.1% Tween solution for 1 hour.
Probe membranes overnight with primary antibodies, including Ascl1, Histone H3, α-Tubulin, LaminB, and Huwe1.
Use mouse or rabbit secondary antibodies for detection and develop membranes using ECL Prime or ECL detection reagents.
Seed Cor3-1 cells at 1.5×10^6 in 10 cm dishes and P19 cells at 1.0×10^6 in 10 cm dishes, transfecting P19 with Ascl1 plasmid constructs as needed.
Wash cells with PBS, scrape into 1 ml PBS, and pellet cells at 1,200 rpm at 4°C for 3 minutes.
Resuspend pellets in ice-cold E1 buffer with protease inhibitor cocktail, pipette gently, and centrifuge to separate cytoplasmic and nuclear fractions.
Sonicate the chromatin fraction in Bioruptor or digest with Benzonase for TUBEs pull down.
Perform Agarose-TUBEs pull down to isolate ubiquitylated proteins from cytoplasm and chromatin fractions.
Incubate with Agarose-TUBEs for 1 hour at 4°C on a rocker platform, then wash and boil in reducing sample buffer.
Treat Cor3-1 or transfected P19 cells with cycloheximide and harvest at defined time points for protein stability assay.
Separate lysates on SDS-PAGE, immunoblot with anti-Ascl1 and anti-α-Tubulin, and quantify protein levels using FiJi software.
Plate Cor3-1 or P19 cells onto ECM-coated 24-well plates and fix in 4% paraformaldehyde at room temperature.
Wash, permeabilise, and block cells before incubating with anti-Ascl1 primary antibody overnight at 4°C.
Incubate cells with Alexa488 goat anti-rabbit IgG secondary antibody for 1 hour at room temperature in the dark.
Stain cells with DAPI, wash, and visualise fluorescence labelling with Axio Scan.
Plate P19 cells into 48-well plates and transfect with ΔM short-Luciferase, pRL-TK, and Ascl1 using Lipofectamine 2000.
Harvest one set of cells the day after transfection and another set after transferring to differentiation media and harvesting 24 hours later.
Perform the Dual-Luciferase Reporter Assay and normalise Luciferase values to Renilla-Luciferase values.
Obtain ethics approval for the use of human specimens from the Ethics Reviewing Board of the University Hospital of Liege, Belgium (ref. 2020/119).
Collect lung postmortem biopsy specimens from four patients who died from SARS-CoV-2 infection and four patients who died from a COVID-19–unrelated cause at the University Hospital of Liege, Belgium.
Select non–COVID-19 lung controls for the best possible match with respect to age and sex.
Obtain postmortem biopsy specimens isolated from the liver, heart, kidney, and pancreas from two COVID-19 patients.
Have all tissues provided by the Biobank of the Liege University Hospital and selected by two pathologists after H&E staining.
Retrospectively analyze hematology and blood biochemistry of COVID-19 patients using the last available blood sample taken in the 24 h preceding the patient’s death.
Fix the samples in formalin and embed in paraffin (FFPE), then cut serial tissue sections of 4 µm for histological and immunofluorescence examination.
Digitize H&E-stained whole slides using a Pannoramic 250 Flash III Scanner (3DHISTECH Ltd.).

Have two experienced pathologists assess high-resolution images focused on immunofluorescence-detected NET areas using a scoring system of lesions typically found in SARS-CoV-2 diffuse alveolar damage.
Deparaffinize and rehydrate lung sections, then boil for 20 min in 10-mM sodium carbonate buffer for antigen retrieval.
Permeabilize lung sections in PBS 0.5% Triton X-100.
Incubate samples with a blocking buffer (PBS with 2% BSA and 2% of donkey serum) for 1 h at room temperature.
Stain samples in blocking buffer with rabbit anti-human antibodies against citrullinated histone H3 and goat anti-human antibodies against MPO for 1 h at room temperature.
Wash samples with PBS and add secondary antibodies conjugated with Alexa Fluor dyes and DAPI, then incubate for 2 h in the dark at room temperature.
Mount samples with ProLong Antifade reagent on glass slides and store at room temperature in the dark overnight.
Analyze all samples by fluorescence microscopy using standard filter sets.
Acquire images on a Zeiss LSM 880 Airyscan Elyra S.1. confocal microscope and process using ImageJ software.

Quantify the volume of NETs present in the lung tissue by analyzing six fields per patient, acquiring Z-stack pictures, and using Imaris software for three-dimensional reconstruction and volume quantification.
Scan entire lung sections using the Nanozoomer 2.0-HT system and manually screen for areas rich in structures staining double positive for Cit-H3 and MPO.
Analyze data for statistical significance using a nonparametric Mann–Whitney U test on mean values.

steps: Germinate four-week-old tomato plants (Solanum lycopersicum Mill. cv. Ailsa Craig) in vermiculite in a growth chamber with a light/dark cycle of 16/8h, temperature of 24/18 °C, light intensity of 200 μmol m–2 s–1, and relative humidity of 60%.
Irrigate seeds twice a week with distilled water.

Irrigate seedlings for 3 weeks with Hoagland solution (control plants) or with Hoagland solution lacking N complemented with 20mM KNO3– (NO3– plants), or 2, 5, or 8mM NH4+ [(NH4)2SO4] (N-NH4+ plants).
Add K2SO4 and CaSO4 to compensate for the absence of K+ and Ca2+ in the nutrient solution.
Adjust the pH of the nutrient solution to 6.0 with 1mM KOH.
Dissolve difluoromethylarginine (DFMA) and difluoromethylornithine (DFMO) in water to create an inhibitor solution containing 2mM DFMA and 5mM DFMO.
Apply the inhibitor solution directly to each pot during the week prior to Pst inoculation.
Treat 4-week-old plants with 0.5mM Put or mock solution (water) using foliar sprays applied 48h before Pst infection.
Grow Pst in King’s B (KB) medium at 28 °C with rifampicin at a concentration of 50mg ml–1.
Grow the coronatine-less strain of Pst (CmaA) (COR–) in KB medium with rifampicin (50mg ml–1) and kanamycin (25mg ml–1).
Adjust bacterial suspensions to 5×105 colony-forming units (cfu) ml–1 in sterile MgSO4 (10mM) containing 0.01% of the surfactant Silwet L-77.
Inoculate plants by dipping the third and fourth leaves into the bacterial suspension.
Score the disease rate at 72h post-inoculation (hpi) by determining the percentage of dark-brown spots on the leaf surface.
Collect samples for molecular and hormonal analyses at 3, 24, and 48 hpi.
Culture Botrytis cinerea CECT2100 on potato dextrose agar at 24 °C.
Collect B. cinerea spores from 10- to 15-day-old cultures with sterile water containing 0.01% (v/v) Tween-20, filter, quantify with a haemacytometer, and adjust at 1×106 ml–1.
Collect and dry four-week-old tomato plants (control and N-NH4+ plants) in an oven for 2 days at 65 ºC.
Weigh dried plant tissues and obtain the dry weight (DW) of 10 plants to express as biomass.
Measure the chlorophyll level of the leaves using a chlorophyll meter (SPDA; Minolta, Tokyo, Japan).
Take three measurements per leaf on each side of the central vein, with 10 plants per treatment, and average the three SPAD readings to represent one observation.
Use an LCpro+ portable infrared gas analyser to measure the net photosynthetic rate (AN) under ambient CO2 and humidity with supplemental light and air flow.
Collect samples of 10 leaves for 3′,3-diaminobenzidine (DAB) staining at 3, 24, and 48 hpi.
Stain leaves with 1mg ml–1 DAB at pH <3 for 24h in the dark, destain in 96% ethanol, and rehydrate in distilled water.
Quantify DAB staining intensities in micrographies using the GIMP program.
Float ten leaf discs (0.5cm2) on 1ml of distilled water for 1h, centrifuge for 1min at 12 000g, and add 100 μl of supernatant to 1ml of xylenol orange assay reagent.
Incubate the mixture for 30min at room temperature and generate a standard curve for H2O2.
Quantify H2O2 by measuring the A560 using a spectrophotometer.
Extract RNA samples from leaf tissue using the E.Z.N.A.® Plant RNA Kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Digest a total of 1.5 μg of total RNA with RNase-free DNase and incubate.
Perform reverse transcription using the Omniscript reverse transcriptase kit.
Carry out quantitative PCR using the Smart Cycler II instrument with the appropriate primers and SYBR Green PCR reaction buffer.
Analyze stomatal aperture by creating a cast with nail polish on a dental resin mould and examining it by light microscopy.
Take images of random regions using a Leica IRB microscope and analyze the stomatal aperture using the Eclipse-Net software.
Freeze fresh material in liquid nitrogen, grind, and freeze dry for hormonal analysis.
Homogenize fresh tissue in ultrapure water with a mixture of internal standards prior to extraction.
Inject a 20 μl aliquot into the HPLC system for hormonal and PA analysis.
Carry out analyses using a Waters Alliance 2690 HPLC system interfaced to a Quatro LC mass spectrometer.
Process quantitative data using the MASSLYNX NT software version 4.1.

Perform statistical analysis using a one-way analysis of variance in the Statgraphics-plus software and compare means using a Fisher’s least-significant difference test at the 95% confidence interval.

steps.action: Replace the fliG gene on the chromosome with a pHluorin(M153R)-fliG allele using the λ Red homologous recombination system.
Prepare L broth (LB) and T broth (TB) as previously described.
Add ampicillin and arabinose to the medium at final concentrations of 100 µg/ml and 0.02% (wt/vol), respectively.
Carry out DNA manipulations as previously described.
Perform DNA sequencing reactions using BigDye v3.1 following the manufacturer’s instructions and analyze the reaction mixtures with a 3130 Genetic Analyzer.
Grow Salmonella cells in 5 ml of LB with shaking at 30°C until the OD600 reaches ~1.0.
Centrifuge the cells at low speed, wash twice with motility buffer, and resuspend in the same buffer.
Incubate the cell suspension at 30°C for 1 hour.
Centrifuge the cultures to separate cell pellets and culture supernatants.
Resuspend cell pellets in SDS loading buffer.
Precipitate proteins in the culture supernatants with 10% trichloroacetic acid, resuspend in Tris-SDS loading buffer, and heat at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Perform SDS-PAGE and immunoblotting with polyclonal anti-FlgD and anti-FliC antibodies.
Purify pHluorin(M153R) from the soluble fractions of BL21(DE3)pLysS carrying pYVM007.
Purify pHluorin(M153R)-FliG-His by Ni-NTA affinity chromatography from the soluble fractions of BL21(DE3)pLysS carrying pYVM013.
Observe Salmonella cells expressing pHluorin(M153R) variants under a custom-built fluorescence microscope with specified settings and filters.
Capture fluorescent images with an EMCCD camera controlled by MetaMorph 3.6 software.
Determine the bulk and local cytoplasmic pH from the ratio of fluorescence intensity in the 410-nm and 470-nm excitation wavelength images.
Subtract the total background intensity from the fluorescence intensity of the cell body to define the fluorescence intensity.
Smooth each fluorescence image by processing over a 7 by 7 pixel area.
Determine pH using a standard curve obtained from purified pHluorin(M153R) or pHluorin(M153R)-FliG.
Capture each fluorescence image with a 5-s exposure to determine the local pH around the export apparatus.
Fit the intensity distribution with a 2D Gaussian function to determine the background threshold.
Measure the 410/470 ratio of purified pHluorin(M153R)-FliG-His at different pH values to prepare a calibration curve.
Perform in vivo calibration using Salmonella flhDC deletion strain transformed with pYVM008 and suspended in motility buffer at various pH values.
Prepare hook-basal bodies (HBBs) from Salmonella strains as previously described.
Apply a 3-μl solution of HBB onto a glow-discharged holey carbon grid and quick-freeze in liquid ethane using Vitrobot.
Collect cryo-EM images and determine defocus and astigmatism using CTFFIND3.
Box out HBB images with BOXER and process them with REFINE2D.PY program for alignment, classification, and averaging.
Carry out 3D image reconstitution of the wild-type and pHluorin(M153R)-labeled HBB structures using the REFINE program with c100 symmetry.
Prepare minicells from the wild-type strain and the ΔfliH-fliI flhB(P28T) bypass mutant.
Collect images of the minicells at liquid-nitrogen temperature using a Titan Krios electron microscope with a Falcon detector.
Bin images 2-fold and calculate 3D reconstructions using the IMOD software package.
Obtain primary human astrocytes from ScienCell Research Laboratories and expand them in Human Astrocyte Media supplemented with FBS, penicillin streptomycin, and Astrocyte Growth Supplement.
Prior to experiments, culture astrocytes in a 50:50 mix of F10:MEMα media supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin streptomycin.
Treat astrocytes with 11 μg/ml of an IGF1R-specific monoclonal antibody, MAB391, for 24 hours.
Wash treated astrocytes with 1× PBS and culture for a further 72 hours in fresh F10:MEMα media.
Include an IgG isotype control, MAB002, in the experiment.
Grow LUHMES in cell culture flasks in proliferation medium until 50-60% confluent.
Differentiate LUHMES by replacing media with differentiation media and culture for 5 days.
Transduce low passage proliferating LUHMES with LV-GFP for 24 hours.
Replace media with fresh proliferation media after transduction and culture for a further 72 hours.
Culture fibroblasts in Minimum essential medium supplemented with 10% FBS, 1% P/S, 1% MEM non-essential amino acids, 1% MEM vitamins, 1% sodium pyruvate, and 60 μg/ml uridine.
Seed astrocytes onto fibronectin-coated 24-well plates and add differentiation media to LUHMES.
Two days later, replate LUHMES onto astrocytes and grow in differentiation media for 24 hours.
Culture LUHMES in astrocyte conditioned media and neuron-astrocyte conditioned media to assess astrocyte support.
Set up fibroblast-LUHMES co-culture system with fibroblasts seeded onto fibronectin-coated plates.
Treat astrocytes with MAB391 or MAB002 for 24 hours, then replate GFP LUHMES onto treated astrocytes and maintain in differentiation media for 72 hours.
Treat co-cultures with 50 μM H2O2 for 2 hours.
Remove medium, wash cells with ice-cold PBS, and lyse cells in extra strong lysis buffer.
Incubate lysates on ice for 25 minutes, sonicate, and centrifuge at 17,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Determine protein concentration using a BCA protein assay kit.
Load 40 μg of protein onto SDS-PAGE gels and transfer to nitrocellulose membrane.
Block membranes and probe with primary antibodies, then with HRP-conjugated secondary antibodies and detect with ECL.
Fix cells in paraformaldehyde, permeabilize, block and incubate with primary antibodies.
Incubate with Alexa-fluor-conjugated secondary antibodies and stain nuclei with Hoechst 33342.
Capture images using a microscope with a camera.
Perform MTT assays to determine a sublethal concentration of H2O2.
Co-culture GFP LUHMES with astrocytes, fix, permeabilize, block, and stain nuclei.
Capture images and measure neurite length using ImageJ plugin Simple Neurite Tracer.
Sort MAB391/IgG-treated astrocytes co-cultured with GFP LUHMES using FACS.
Collect cells, centrifuge, and resuspend in TRIzol for PCR analysis.
Isolate RNA from FACS sorted cells and perform reverse transcription.
Perform PCR and run samples on an agarose gel, then image the gel.
Produce amplified, fragmented, and labeled ss-cDNA from total RNA using the GeneChip WT PLUS reagent kit.
Hybridize ss-cDNA to GeneChip Human Gene ST Arrays and perform washing and staining.
Scan gene chips and assess data quality using the expression console software.
Normalize data using RMA and perform principal component analysis to eliminate sample outliers.

steps: Enrich A-CD8+ T cells (2 x 10^6 cells) from individual A.
Stimulate the enriched A-CD8+ T cells with B-APCs (1 x 10^6 cells) from individual B (HLA-A, -B, -DR mismatched with individual A) in 24-well plates.
Add IL-2 (20 U/ml), IL-7 (50 ng/ml), and IL-15 (50 ng/ml) to the culture.
Incubate for 9 days to allow for the expansion of CD8+ CD28- T cells.
Enrich the in vitro-expanded CD8+ CD28- T cells after incubation.
Label A-CD4+ T cells (5 x 10^4/well) from individual A with CFSE.
Coculture CFSE-labeled A-CD4+ T cells with either B-APCs (5 x 10^4/well) or I-APCs (5 x 10^4/well) from individual I (HLA-A, -B, and -DR fully mismatched with individual A and B).
Add in vitro-expanded CD8+ CD28- T cells (2.5 x 10^4/well) to the coculture in a 96-well round bottom plate.
Incubate the cocultures for 7 days and 11 days.
Assess the proliferation of A-CD4+ T cells using CFSE dilution assay.
Administer a mixture of human cells into NOG mice by intraperitoneal injection for in vivo experiments.
Sacrifice the mice 11 days after injection.
Investigate human CD4+ T cells in the spleen of mice by flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry to determine the state of immunosuppression.
Examine the proliferative capacity of CD8+ CD28+ T cells and CD8+ CD28- T cells by APC stimulation in the presence of common gamma chain cytokines for 9 days using CFSE dilution.
Purify CD8+ CD28+ T cells and incubate them in a coculture system with the common gamma chain cytokines to observe the transformation to CD8+ CD28- T cells.
Evaluate cell survival by staining with Annexin V and compare the necrotic rate of CD8+ T cells with and without cytokine stimulation over 9 days.
Compare the expression of cytokine receptors on in vitro-expanded CD8+ CD28- T cells with freshly purified cells.
Analyze the expression of immunomodulatory molecules and cytotoxic function markers on CD8+ CD28- T cells before and after in vitro expansion.

steps.action: Sow Phaseolus vulgaris seeds in vermiculite.
Grow seedlings in a growth chamber at 23°C with a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle and 75% relative humidity.
Cultivate seedlings in plastic pots filled with moist vermiculite for 10–12 days until primary leaves are fully-expanded.
Transplant three seedlings into a 20 cm plastic pot with moist vermiculite.
Place the pots with seedlings in a dark room 24 h prior to inoculation.
For genetic mapping, phenotype the 77 F11 RILs 7 days post-inoculation.
Construct BPMV-derived vectors by inserting P. vulgaris target gene fragments into the BamH1 restriction site of pBPMV-IA-V1.
Amplify target gene fragments by PCR using specific primers and P. vulgaris cDNAs as template.
Digest PCR products with BamH1 and insert into BamH1-digested and dephosphorylated pBPMV-IA-V1.
Determine the orientation of the cloned inserts by PCR using vector-specific and fragment-specific primers.
Sequence clones with inserted fragments in the antisense orientation to confirm their identity.
Prepare a DNA-plasmid mix in 20 μL of 50 mM potassium phosphate buffer, pH 7.0, for primary inoculation.
For secondary inoculations, grind an infected leaf of P. vulgaris cv. Black Valentine in mock buffer to make leaf sap.
Perform inoculations by mechanical rubbing of one primary leaf.
Grow inoculated plants at 19°C under a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle in a growth chamber.
Prepare a 20 μL plasmid DNA mix containing equal amounts of pBPMV-IA-R1M and either pBPMV-IA-V1 or pBPMV-GFP2.
Evaluate three intensities of rubbing for inoculation: low, medium, and high.
Examine GFP expression using a UV lamp and photograph using a digital camera.
Perform microscopic observations of roots at 21 dpi and photograph using a microscope camera.
Extract total RNA and synthesize cDNA as described.
Perform semi-quantitative RT-PCR with specific primers for the PvPDS gene and PvUBI as a control.
Analyse PCR products using analytical agarose-ethidium bromide electrophoresis.
Use a Chi-squared test to evaluate the goodness of fit of observed and expected segregation ratios for genetic mapping.
Map the R-BPMV resistance gene using MAPMAKER software and a set of 142 markers.
Establish linkage groups with a LOD threshold of 3.0 and a maximum recombination fraction of 0.3.
Estimate the position of R-BPMV on LG B2 with a LOD threshold of 2.0 using the 'try' function.
Estimate map distances using the Kosambi mapping function.
Obtain 166 blood samples from 41 patients admitted to the Prince of Wales Hospital, Hong Kong, ensuring all patients meet the World Health Organization criteria for a probable case of SARS.
Culture all cell lines in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) with Glutamax and high glucose, supplemented with 10% fetal calf serum and penicillin/streptomycin.
Clone the gene encoding human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) from a human primary kidney cDNA library using 21-mer primers designed to the start and stop of ACE2.
Subclone the ACE2 gene into pcdna3.1+.
Transfect QT6 cells with the ACE2 construct using lipofectamine 2000.
Select transfected QT6 cells with G418 and grow a bulk ACE2-positive, G418-resistant population.
Split confluent plates of 293T cells 1:4 the day before transfection.
Transfect each plate of 293T cells with 1 μg gag/pol construct, 1.5 μg of enhanced GFP reporter construct, and 1.5 μg envelope-expressing construct using Fugene-6 transfection reagent.
Harvest supernatant from the transfected 293T cells 48 h and 72 h post-transfection.
Filter the harvested supernatant through 0.45-μm filters and store at –80°C.
Measure MLV and HIV vector titer on 293T, TE671, and QT6/ACE2 cells, presenting the results as infectious units (IU) per milliliter.
Infect cells with vector and determine eGFP titers 72 h later by fluorescence-activated cell sorter (FACS).
Heat inactivate patient serum samples at 56°C for 30 min.
Serially dilute the heat-inactivated serum samples from 1:10 in culture medium.
Add 50 PFU of SARS Frankfurt strain to the serum dilution and incubate for 1 h at 37°C.
Add 5 × 10^4 Vero E6 cells per well to the virus and serum mix.
Incubate the mixture in 96-well plates for 4 days and assess neutralization by cytopathic effect (CPE).
Determine the neutralization endpoint as the last well in which complete neutralization is observed.
Assay serum samples in duplicate and confirm positive results in separate assays.
For pseudotype neutralization assays, mix heat-inactivated serum samples with MLV(SARS) virions at a 1:1 vol/vol ratio after 2-fold serial dilution.
Incubate the serum and virion mixture at 37°C for 1 h.
Add 100 μL of each dilution to QT6/ACE2 cells seeded at 1 × 10^4 cells per well in 96-well flat-bottomed tissue culture plates seeded 24 h previously.
Count GFP-positive cells 48 h later by fluorescence microscopy.
Present neutralizing antibody titers as geometric mean titers of assays performed in triplicate.

steps: 1. Cross Arabidopsis stn1 mutants derived from ecotypes with short (Col-0, 2–4 kb) and long (Ws, 4–8 kb) telomeres to generate stn1 (W/C) mutants.
2. Observe the first generation (G1) stn1 (W/C) mutants for mild growth defects and a low frequency of anaphase bridges.
3. Monitor the severity of growth defects and genome instability in subsequent generations (G2 and G3) of stn1 (W/C) mutants.
4. Quantitatively describe the occurrence of defects by dividing plants into five phenotypic categories from wt-looking plants (wt) to stunted plants unable to produce seeds (terminal).
5. Measure the telomere length of G1 stn1 (C) and stn1 (W/C) mutants.
6. Perform dot blot hybridization to quantify the amount of telomeric DNA in G2 and G3 stn1 (C) mutants.
7. Analyze exo1a exo1b stn1 mutants to assess the effect of EXO1 on STN1-null telomeres.
8. Observe the developmental defects in G1 exo1 stn1 mutants and compare them to G1 stn1 mutants.
9. Record the frequency of anaphase bridges and developmental defects in G2 exo1 stn1 mutants.
10. Measure the expression levels of DNA repair genes including PARP1 and BRCA1 in exo1 stn1 plants.
11. Conduct terminal restriction fragment (TRF) analysis and dot-blot hybridization to compare telomere length and heterogeneity between stn1 and exo1 stn1 mutants.
12. Compare the relative G-overhang size in stn1 and exo1 stn1 plants using the in gel hybridization technique.
13. Quantify the frequency of telomeric permutations forming the chromosome termini in stn1 and exo1 stn1 mutants by adaptor ligation-mediated PCR coupled with Illumina sequencing.
14. Generate telomerase-null stn1 and exo1 stn1 mutants by disrupting the TERT gene.
15. Compare the growth defects between stn1 tert and exo1 stn1 tert mutants.
16. Analyze the telomere length among siblings outsegregating from STN1+/− TERT+/− and exo1 STN1+/− TERT+/− parents.
17. Perform an in gel hybridization assay to test whether telomerase activity contributes to the elongated G-overhangs in stn1 mutants.
18. Analyze plants carrying hypomorphic mutations in the catalytic subunit of DNA polymerase α (pol α and icu2-1).
19. Conduct cytogenetic analysis to detect anaphase bridges in pol α and icu2-1 mutants.
20. Use a fusion PCR strategy with primers specific to subtelomeric regions to detect chromosome-end-to-end fusions.
21. Perform the t-circle amplification assay to analyze t-circle abundance in DNA polymerase α mutants.
22. Carry out TRF analysis to assess the impact of DNA polymerase α mutations on telomere maintenance.
23. Determine the relative size of the telomeric G-overhangs in pol α and icu2-1 mutants using in gel hybridizations.
24. Detect blunt-ended telomeres in pol α and icu2-1 mutants by the hairpin ligation assay followed by alkaline gel electrophoresis.
25. Sequence the telomeric blunt-ends by Illumina sequencing to analyze the frequency of specific telomeric permutations.
26. Generate stn1 atxr5 atxr6 plants to test the role of STN1 in genome-wide replication.
27. Measure the nuclear DNA content in stn1 atxr5 atxr6 plants by flow cytometry.
28. Induce chronic genotoxic stress in Arabidopsis seedlings with bleomycin and measure PARP1 expression levels.
29. Quantitatively measure DNA re-replication by analyzing the shape of 8C peaks detected by flow cytometry.
30. Use Illumina sequencing to analyze genomic DNA from sorted 8C nuclei and quantify the density of reads mapped along the individual Arabidopsis chromosomes.

steps.action: Collect mRNA levels of MCU and related proteins (MCUb, MICU1-3, and EMRE) from the TCGA breast cancer dataset.
Analyze data relative to tumor size and regional lymph node infiltration to determine correlation with MCU and MCUb expression levels.
Select three different human metastatic TNBC cell lines: BT-549, MDA-MB-468, and MDA-MB-231.
Choose an agonist for each cell line that evokes a robust cytosolic Ca2+ transient (ATP for MDA-MB-231 and MDA-MB-468, histamine for BT-549 cells).
Perform siRNA-mediated inhibition of MCU in all three cell models and measure the decline in agonist-induced mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake.
Conduct a wound healing migration assay to monitor cell motility impairment due to MCU silencing in all TNBC lines.
Measure cytosolic Ca2+ transients, SOCE, and ER Ca2+ content to determine the effects of MCU silencing.
Overexpress MCU in the three cell lines and measure the increase in agonist-induced mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake and the decrease in cytosolic Ca2+ transients.
Perform an in vitro spheroid formation assay with stable MCU-silenced cells to investigate their invasion potential.
Grow shMCU cells in agar containing medium, then transfer spheroid-shaped colonies into a collagen matrix and monitor their migration.
Conduct a colony formation assay to assess cell growth inhibition by shMCU over 7 days.
Measure mitochondrial membrane potential (∆Ψ) using the cationic fluorescent dye TMRM.
Achieve MCU deletion in MDA-MB-231 cells using CRISPR/Cas9 Nuclease RNA-guided genome editing technology.
Inject MCU−/− cells into the fat pad of SCID mice and measure tumor growth, lymph node infiltration, and metastasis formation.
Sacrifice mice at different time points to compare metastatic potential of tumors with equal size.
Measure cellular and mitochondrial NADH levels, NADPH levels, and ATP production using live cell fluorescent and luminescent techniques.
Assess cellular NADPH/NADH homeostasis by measuring the fluorescence lifetime parameters (τbound).
Compare resting NADH fluorescence intensity to maximally oxidized and maximally reduced states.
Measure ATP production rate after 2-deoxy-D-glucose treatment in MCU-silenced and control cells.
Treat MDA-MB-231 cells with antioxidants (NAC and DTE) and the mitochondria-targeted ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO to analyze their effects on cell migration.
Directly measure mitochondrial H2O2 levels with pHyper-dMito protein sensor and mitochondrial pH with SypHer2 sensor.
Use HyPerRed probe and MitoSOX™ dye to confirm the reduction in mitochondrial ROS levels.
Express mitGrx1-roGFP2 sensor in cells to detect mitochondrial glutathione redox potential (EGSH) and oxidative stress.
Investigate the effect of MCU silencing on HIF-1α protein levels and its regulation.
Treat cells with the proteasome inhibitor MG132 and monitor levels of HIF-1α and hydroxylated HIF-1α.
Assess HIF1A and HIF2A transcription levels following MCU silencing in both normoxic and hypoxic conditions.
Measure transcription levels of HIF-1α target genes involved in metabolic reprogramming and migration control.
Perform rescue experiments by re-expressing HIF-1α in MCU-silenced cells to determine its effect on cell migration.
Analyze the mRNA levels of HIF-1α and its regulated genes in the TCGA BRCA dataset to correlate with MCU expression.
Stain the cell suspension of planaria with Hoechst 33342 (nuclear dye) and MTG (mitochondrial dye).
Identify three distinct cell populations based on nuclear content: X1, X2, and Xins.
Treat cells with Verapamil (an efflux pump inhibitor) and stain with MTG to test for dye efflux.
Generate and characterize an antibody to PIWI-1.
Perform immunostaining with PIWI-1 antibody on planarian cells to identify PIWI-1 High, Low, and negative cells.
Examine the expression of PIWI-1 in MTG High and MTG Low cells within the X1 population.
Perform RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) on X1-MTG Low and X1-MTG High populations.
Analyze differential expression using Cuffdiff and perform Gene Ontology (GO) analysis.
Compare differentially expressed genes with published single-cell transcriptome data.
Subject X2 population cells with low and high MTG signals to PIWI-1 immunostaining and transcriptome analysis.
Sort X2-MTG Low and X2-MTG High cells based on size (FSC) to obtain four populations.
Perform RNA-seq on the four sorted X2 populations and analyze the data.
Conduct cell cycle analysis on sorted X2-MTG Low cells to determine their phase.
Use SiR-DNA dye to isolate 4N and 2N cells from asexual planarians and stain with MTG.
Transplant sorted cell populations into lethally irradiated animals for piwi-1 colony expansion assay and survival studies.
Assay transplanted animals for the presence of piwi-1+ colonies after 8 days posttransplantation.
Perform survival studies on transplanted and nontransplanted animals post lethal dose of irradiation.
Stain planarian cells with MTG and MitoTracker Orange (MTO) to assess mitochondrial membrane potential.
Treat regenerating worms with FCCP to investigate the effect on stem cell differentiation.
Perform RNA FISH and qPCR analysis for piwi-1 on control and FCCP-treated worms.
Culture neoblasts, treat them with FCCP, and assess PIWI-1 expression.
Perform transplantation assays with FCCP-treated neoblasts to validate their stemness.
Cross fluorescence reporter mice Pax2-Cre line with R26R-Lyn-Venus line for live-imaging analysis or use ICR mice for other experiments.
Designate the midnight preceding the plug as E0.0.
Sacrifice mice by cervical dislocation at E15.5 or E16.5 to minimize suffering.
Fix dissected epididymides with 4% PFA in PBS for 2 hours at 4°C or for 20 minutes at 37°C, or with 2% TCA in Ca2+- and Mg2+-free PBS for 20 minutes at 4°C, depending on target epitopes.
Block samples by incubation in 10% normal goat serum or 10% normal donkey serum diluted in 0.1% Triton X-100/PBS for 3 hours at 37°C, depending on the secondary antibody species.
Treat samples with primary antibodies overnight at 4°C.
Incubate samples with secondary antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor 546 or Alexa Fluor 647 overnight at 4°C.
Use TRITC-conjugated phalloidin and Hoechst 33342 for visualization of F-actin and DNA, respectively.
Mount samples with 1% agarose gel on a glass-based dish for stable imaging.
Immerse samples with BABB solution or CUBIC2 solution for optical clearing.
Obtain 8-bit volumetric fluorescence images using a confocal laser-scanning platform with appropriate objective lens magnifications.
Surgically excise epididymides and place on a hydrophilic polytetrafluoroethylene organ culture insert in a Petri dish filled with culture medium.
Culture samples in an air-liquid interface at 37°C under 5% CO2.
Use small-molecule inhibitors such as blebbistatin, Y-27632, and mitomycin C as required.
Perform live imaging under modified organ culture conditions using an incubator-integrated multiphoton fluorescence microscope.
Expose PDMS chamber to plasma arc for hydrophilic treatment for tissue compression assay.
Place isolated epididymides onto hydrophilized PDMS chamber and fill with type I collagen.
Compress epididymides with collagen gel by relaxing from the 50% stretched state.
Incubate samples for morphological confirmation analysis and western blotting analysis.
Extract total protein from each treatment and adjust the amount for SDS-PAGE.
Determine protein concentration of the supernatant by bicinchoninic acid assay.
Prepare lysates for SDS-PAGE and perform electrophoresis.
Blot proteins onto polyvinylidene difluoride membrane and block with H2O2/TBS solution and NGS.
Incubate membranes with primary antibodies overnight at 4°C.
Incubate membranes with secondary antibody solutions at 37°C for 60 minutes.
Detect protein bands using Western Blotting Detection Reagent and scan with ImageQuant LAS 4000.
Perform statistical hypothesis testing and replicate experiments more than three times.
Use MATLAB and ImageJ for digital image processing and MATLAB, R, Gnuplot, and Paraview for graphics and statistical analysis.
Scan each cloned HAG maize CoREG for the presence of an acetyl-CoA-binding site using the Conserved Domain Database (CDD).
Use the identified region (approximately 75–90 amino acids) as the operational taxonomic unit for phylogenetic analysis.
Align related proteins using ClustalW with default parameters implemented using the megalign program within the dnastar Lasergene package.
For AUX/IAA CoREGs, align FL amino acid sequences using MUSCLE with default parameters.
Export each multiple sequence alignment in Newick format.
Display phylogenetic trees using FigTree V1.4.0.
Clone constructs into either the pENTR/D-TOPO or pENTR/SD/D-TOPO vector.
Amplify targeted TF or CoREG ORFs using high-fidelity Phusion polymerase with the manufacturer's GC buffer supplemented with 10% glycerol.
Optimize PCR conditions by adding up to 10% DMSO, up to 4 mM MgCl2, or adjusting the annealing temperature as needed.
Design primers to produce a fragment without a stop codon and with a 5'-CACC nucleotide tailing added to the forward primer for directional cloning.
Screen kanamycin-resistant colonies for inserts of the correct size and orientation by colony PCR or restriction digestion.
Confirm the sequence of cloned inserts by single-read paired-end Sanger dideoxy sequencing.
Design internal primers to complete the sequence confirmation for clones longer than 1200 bp.
Grow B73 inbred maize in a field nursery and isolate DNA for PCR amplification of single-exon genes or RNA for RT-PCR.
Receive pENTRSD/D-TOPO clones harboring synthesized coding sequences (CDSs) optimized according to maize, yeast, or hybrid preference.

Use LR Clonase to recombine these CDSs into a GAL4-BD-GWC1 vector to fuse them with the yeast GAL4-binding domain (BD), or to generate N-terminal fusions with GFP into plasmid p1511 under the control of the 35S promoter.
Transform PJ69.4a yeast cells with each GAL4-BD-GWC1 construct using the lithium acetate/single-stranded carrier DNA/polyethylene glycol method.
Grow cells in synthetic medium without tryptophan at 30°C to OD600 = 0.6, centrifuge, resuspend in water and NaOH, incubate, centrifuge again, and resuspend in SDS loading buffer.
Heat the resuspended cells to 95°C for 5 min, centrifuge, and load the extract for analysis by 10% SDS-PAGE.
Block the membrane for Western blot analysis, incubate with primary antibody, wash, incubate with secondary antibody, wash, and expose for protein detection.
Chop and digest second or third leaves from 13-day-old B73 × Mo17 F1 hybrid etiolated seedlings for protoplast preparation.
Filter protoplasts through a 35-μm nylon mesh, centrifuge, wash in ES buffer, and count with a hemocytometer.
Carry out electroporation on protoplasts with DNA for transient assays using a BTX Electro-Square-Porator T820.
Incubate protoplasts post-electroporation for 18–22 h in the dark at room temperature.
Estimate transformation efficiency by GFP expression analysis using fluorescence microscopy and Image J software.
Isolate genomic DNA from B73 plant tissue using a CTAB-based method.
Isolate total RNA from non-starchy B73 tissues using RNAzol according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Employ a modified protocol for RNA isolation from starchy tissues such as developing seeds.
Verify RNA integrity by agarose gel electrophoresis and ethidium bromide staining.
Treat total RNA samples with Turbo DNA-free to remove any contaminating DNA.
Synthesize cDNA using Maxima H Minus Reverse Transcriptase according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Determine the integrity of cDNA by amplifying a portion of a ZmGAPDH transcript and confirming the absence of genomic DNA.
Amplify TFs by RT-PCR from tissues where they are most highly expressed, as determined from the RNA-Seq dataset stored at the qTeller database.

steps.description: Input sequence to the array design using 300,919 sequences totaling 101.8 Mb, derived from gene models predicted from RNA-Seq reads, barley full-length cDNA, and de novo assembled RNA-Seq contigs.
Assemble RNA-Seq contigs with CLC assembly cell from RNA-Seq reads of different cultivars.
Generate variable length probes (50- to 100-mers) at a 5-bp step across the entire sequence space.
Repeat-mask individual probes by removing those with an average 15-mer frequency >200, using a 15-mer frequency table from the Morex genome assembly.
Compare the repeat-masked probe set back to the target sequence using SSAHA with a minimum match size of 30 and allowing up to five indels or gaps.
Eliminate probe sequences with more than 25 matches in the target set from consideration.
Generate a probe set containing 2,040,943 unique probes by selecting them at an average spacing of 40 bp.
Create an array design using two replicates of the probe set and two replicates of a set of 77,192 random probes.
Hybridize two slides of the array design for 4 days with four barley cultivars using standard CGH protocols.
Remove 0.42% of the probes as missed repetitive elements based on high signal intensity from the CGH results.
Exclude an additional 2.16% of the probes as contaminants or non-performing based on low signal for all four cultivars.
Use the remaining probes to construct a solution-phase capture pool.
Capture and sequence four cultivars using standard protocols with an Illumina HiSeq (2×76 bp).
Optimize empirically the capture design using sequencing data and a proprietary Roche NimbleGen method.
Prepare Illumina TruSeq Paired End libraries using DNA Adapter Indexes 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, or 12.
Fragment 1 μg genomic DNA into a 200–300 bp size range using Covaris microTUBES and a Covaris S220 Instrument.
Recover DNA adapter ligated products with a size between 320 and 420 bp by excision from an SYBR-Gold stained agarose gel if size fractionation is used.
Purify the TruSeq DNA libraries using AmPure XP Beads and elute in Resuspension Buffer.
Enrich for correctly ligated DNA fragments using 20 μl of the TruSeq DNA library in a pre-capture LM-PCR reaction.
Quantify the DNA using a Qubit 2.0 fluorometer and analyze electrophoretically with an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer using a DNA 7500 chip.
Add 10 μl of Roche NimbleGen's proprietary Plant Capture Enhancer to a 1.5-ml tube containing 1 μg of the amplified sample library.
Add 1 μl of TS-HE Universal Oligo 1 and 1 μl of the appropriate TS-INV-HE Index Oligo to the tube and dry down the mixture in a SpeedVac at 60°C.
Pool up to six samples with different indexes for hybridization, adjusting the amount of the corresponding TS-INV-HE Index Oligos proportional to the sample concentration.
Add 7.5 μl of 2× Sequence Capture Hybridization Buffer and 3 μl of Hybridization Component A to each dried-down sample.
Denature the hybridization cocktail in a heat block at 95°C for 10 min and transfer to a PCR tube containing Exome Library.
Incubate the hybridization sample in a thermocycler at 47°C for 64–72 h.
Dilute NimbleGen SC Wash Buffers, Stringent Wash Buffer, and Bead Wash Buffer to 1× working solutions.
Prepare Streptavidin Dynabeads for affinity purification of captured DNA.
Bind the captured sample to the Dynabeads in a thermocycler at 47°C for 45 min.
Wash the Dynabeads plus bound DNA with SC Wash Buffer I, Stringent Wash Buffer, and Wash Buffers I, II, and III.
Resuspend the bead-bound captured library in PCR-grade water for storage at −20°C.
Amplify the bead-bound captured library using LM-PCR.
Clean-up the LM-PCR reactions using the Qiaquick PCR purification kit with slight modifications.
Elute DNA after addition of EB, incubation, and centrifugation and record the A260/A280 ratio using a NanoDrop spectrophotometer.
Analyze the library fragments of the post-capture enriched sequencing libraries electrophoretically using the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer and a DNA 7500 chip.
Map target regions derived from transcript contigs against the WGS assembly of barley cultivar ‘Morex’ with BWA and Mega BLAST.
Collapse mapping positions on the assembly into a single bed file with BEDTools.
Map sequencing reads to the Morex assembly with BWA, compute coverage with SAMtools depth, and calculate coverage statistics with AWK scripts.
Visualize coverage statistics in the R statistical environment.
Perform regression analysis of sequencing output, read coverage, and the number of detected SNPs using standard R functions.
Compare regions with high coverage but not located within target regions with targets using Mega BLAST and filter BLAST output with an AWK script.
Perform SNP calling with SAMtools mpileup/BCFtools using default parameters.
Filter resulting SNP calls with a custom AWK script discarding positions with quality score below 40 or coverage below 10-fold.
Visualize SNP frequency along the integrated physical and genetic map of barley with an R script.
Quality trim and assemble sequencing reads from H. pubiflorum and H. bulbosum with CLC assembly cell using quality_trim and clc_novo_assemble.
Map capture targets against the H. pubiflorum contigs with BWA-SW and define target intervals with BEDTools.
Filter variant positions and genotype calls for phylogenetic tree construction according to specified criteria.
Calculate the Hamming distance between any two samples.
Construct a neighbor-joining tree with the resulting distance matrix using the function nj() in the package 'ape'.

steps: 1. Culture D. coniospora strain ATCC 96282 on solid Nematode Growth Medium (NGM) at 25°C in the presence of C. elegans or in liquid NGM with Yeast extract (NGMY) in the absence of nematodes.
2. For DNA extraction, inoculate roughly 10^9 fresh spores in 100 mL NGMY medium and culture for 7 days.
3. Harvest mycelia by vacuum filtering through a sterile 10 μm nylon membrane.
4. Place the filter in a 30°C incubator for about 3 hours until mycelia are dry.
5. Manually grind the dried mycelia in a liquid nitrogen-cooled mortar.
6. Transfer a 20 mg aliquot of ground mycelia to a 1.5 mL tube.
7. Extract DNA using the DNeasy Plant Mini Kit (Qiagen) following the manufacturer's instructions.
8. For RNA extraction, collect fresh spores from 10 cm NGM plates of infected worms and inoculate in 100 mL of NGMY liquid medium, then culture for 4 days or serially culture for 5 x 8 day cycles.
9. Collect samples by filtering cultures through 0.22 μm Steritop units (Milipore), flash freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at -80°C.
10. Dissolve aliquots of 200 mg of spores or mycelia in 1 mL Trizol (Invitrogen) in lysing matrix tubes (MP Biomedicals).
11. Homogenize for 20 s at 6 m/s in a FastPrep-24 (MP Biomedicals), incubate on ice for 2 min, and homogenize a second time.
12. Purify RNA using a standard protocol and clean with an RNeasy mini Kit (Qiagen).
13. Prepare MIseq paired-end libraries from genomic DNA and sequence on an Illumina MIseq sequencer as 2 x 150 bp paired-end reads following the manufacturer's standard procedures.
14. For SOLiD sequencing, prepare two mate-paired libraries from genomic DNA following the manufacturer's instructions.
15. Shear DNA to 1.5 kb or 3 kb fragments with Covaris System and Covaris Blue miniTUBES.
16. Perform nick-translation for 9.5 min to generate fragments of < 400 bp.
17. Amplify the library through 14 rounds of PCR.
18. Size-select fragments between 250 and 300 bp using 4% acrylamide gel.
19. Purify with SOLiD Library Micro Column Purification Kit prior to conversion for analysis with the 5500 WildFire system (Life Technologies, Carlsbad, USA).
20. Construct cDNA libraries and perform Illumina sequencing of mRNA from spores and mycelia using an Illumina HiSeq 2000 platform at the Beijing Genomics Institute.
21. Process MIseq reads with BBDuk software to filter out contaminants and low quality reads.
22. Use the remaining reads for de novo genome assembly with Velvet, SPAdes, SOAPdenovo2, and ABySS using standard input parameters, except for ABySS which uses k values of 64 and 96.
23. Scaffold the resulting assemblies using SOLiD mate-paired reads with SSPACE v2.0, setting the k parameter to 5.
24. Perform de novo transcriptome assembly on the combined sets of reads from the two sequenced libraries with Trinity using default parameters.
25. Generate a whole genome map of D. coniospora using the Argus Whole-Genome Mapping System and select XbaI using Enzyme Chooser (OpGen Inc.).
26. Sort out molecules longer than 200 kb for assembly with MapSolver software.
27. Manually validate the resulting map contigs leading to 9 maps with a cumulative size of 31.8 Mb.
28. Compare these with the in silico XbaI digestion profile of the scaffolds obtained after sequencing.
29. Perform genome annotation using standard open source software, including RepeatScout, RepeatMasker, TransposonPSI, Rfam scan perl script, and tRNAscan-SE.
30. Predict genes using Augustus trained with Trinity-derived D. coniospora transcripts and Fusarium graminearum, retaining additional predicted proteins that meet specific criteria.
31. Annotate the set of predicted protein-coding genes using Interproscan with various databases and perform the same protocol for eleven additional fungi.
32. Predict signal peptide, target peptide, and transmembrane domains using SignalP, TargetP, and Tmhmm respectively.
33. Perform a Blast analysis versus PHI-base proteins to associate D. coniospora genes with pathogenicity, virulence, and effector genes.
34. Refine the set of BUSCO-defined orthologues and calculate phylogenetic distances using MAFFT and PhyML within the Mobyle Web environment.
35. Plot the output using the tree drawing engine implemented in the ETE toolkit.
36. Compare each D. coniospora protein model to proteins listed in the CAZy database and assign to families based on sequence conservation.
37. Cluster protein families and domains using “One minus Pearson correlation” distance matrices within GENE-E.
38. Carry out secretome analysis by combining predictions from SignalP, WolfPSORT, and NucPred.
39. Determine probable protein localization using TargetP and derive a consensus predicted localization.
40. Identify PFAM domains through a search against the PFAM 28.0 database using gathering thresholds.
41. Align Illumina paired-end RNAseq reads to the genome assembly using STAR and assign reads to gene models using the htseq-count script within HTSeq.
42. Establish lists of differentially regulated genes using previously described methods.
43. Align unaligned RNAseq reads from C. elegans infected with D. coniospora to gene models.
44. Infect N2 worms at the L4 stage with fungal spores on NGMY plates spread with E. coli strain OP50, incubate for 24 h, then culture in NGMY liquid medium for another 30 h.
45. Collect mycelia by filtration and prepare protoplasts.
46. Transform protoplasts using PEG/CaCl2-mediated DNA uptake with expression vectors containing a hygromycin selection marker.
47. Select transformants for antibiotic resistance on medium containing 15 μg/ml hygromycin and screen for fluorescence.
48. Infect worms on NGM plates with spores from SapA::DsRed expressing fungus and culture at 25°C for 15 to 30 days.
49. Harvest spores in 50 mM NaCl, wash extensively in cold 50 mM NaCl, pellet, and resuspend in lysis buffer.
50. Flash-freeze the resuspended spores, sonicate, and vortex with acid-washed glass beads.
51. Use the supernatant from a high-speed centrifugation as a whole protein extract for pull-down assays.
52. Incubate protein extracts with purified His-tagged proteins, immunoprecipitate with anti-dsRed/RFP agarose beads overnight at 4°C.
53. Wash beads, elute in SDS-PAGE loading buffer, resolve on a gradient denaturating PAGE gel, transfer onto a membrane, and probe with antibodies.
54. Visualize blots using enhanced chemiluminescence.
1. Dispense siRNA SMARTpools (0.3 µM, 10 µl volumes) into triplicate black 384-well plates using a Rapidplate384 liquid handler.
2. Seal plates with adhesive seals and plastic lids, then store at -80°C (24-48 h).
3. Thaw assay plates at room temperature on the day of transfection.
4. Add 10 µl transfection reagent (Dharmafect 1, 0.1% final concentration) diluted in HBSS to each well using a Multidrop 384.
5. Incubate plates for 20 min at room temperature to allow transfection complex formation.
6. Wash low-passage Hela cells in PBS and trypsinize with Trypsin-EDTA.
7. Dilute cells in phenol red-free, antibiotic-free transfection medium (DMEM/F-12 1:1/5% FCS with 15 mM Hepes and L-glu).
8. Count cells and add 3x10^3 cells in 40 µl to each well using the Multidrop 384.
9. Incubate plates for 48 h at 37°C in a humidified incubator with 5% CO2.
10. Remove media from plates by inversion and add 10 µl media (with penicillin-streptomycin) or virus (HSV-1-eGFP strain C12, MOI 0.5) using the Multidrop 384.
11. Incubate plates at 37°C for 1 h.
12. Add 50 µl infection media to each well and return plates to the incubator.
13. Monitor replication as a function of eGFP fluorescence from 24 h to 80 h post-infection using a POLARstar OPTIMA plate reader.
14. Calculate and normalize virus replication slopes to mock transfected wells on individual assay plates.
15. Use the mean replication slope from six replicates for subsequent data analyses.
1. Confirm the infectivity of AAV, adenoviral, and lentiviral vectors on embryos.
2. Choose serotype 6 AAV (AAV6) vector based on its infectivity in mouse and human ES cells.
3. Microinject each viral vector encoding EGFP driven by the CAG promoter into the perivitelline space of pronuclear-stage mouse embryos.
4. Confirm the expression of EGFP under a fluorescence microscope at the morula/blastocyst stage.
5. Remove the zona pellucida to enable efficient infection by the lentiviral vector, if necessary.
6. Co-culture embryos with an intact zona pellucida with the viral vectors as a control.
7. Observe efficient infection with the AAV vector in embryos with intact zona pellucida.
8. Confirm that AAV vector dose-dependent transgene expression is high from the 4-cell stage to the morula stage in mouse embryos.
9. Test AAV serotypes other than serotype 6 for transduction efficiency.
10. Examine rat and bovine embryos for AAV transduction efficiency.
11. Infect parthenogenetic embryos with the AAV vector to test the hypothesis of virus passing through the holes created during fertilization.
12. Inject femto-picoliter virus suspension at 1 x 10^8 IU/mL into the perivitelline space of each zygote.
13. Investigate the delivery of donor DNA into embryos by AAV vector for large-fragment knockin using the CRISPR/Cas9 system.
14. Introduce Cas9-RNP into pronuclear-stage embryos by electroporation.
15. Infect with scAAV vector harboring a 1.8-kb CAG-GFP cassette flanked by two 100-bp Rosa26 homology arms.
16. Assess the efficiency of knockin at the Rosa26 locus at the blastocyst stage.
17. Confirm EGFP expression by fluorescence stereomicroscopy and flow cytometry of peripheral blood.
18. Verify correct insertion of the cassette in the Rosa26 locus without indel mutations at the site of junction.
19. Confirm germline transmission by breeding the knockin founders with wild-type mice and genotyping N1 generation offsprings.
20. Perform the same experiment with ssAAV vector harboring a 1.8-kb CAG-GFP cassette flanked by two 1-kb Rosa26 homology arms.
21. Use droplet digital PCR to quantify the number of EGFP inserts and wild-type (un-inserted) Rosa26 alleles per cell.
22. Design gRNAs to target introns surrounding the mutation in exon 3 for the rescue of the nude phenotype by exon exchange.
23. Generate scAAV harboring functional exon 3 flanked by two homology arms.
24. Confirm successful exchange of exon 3 by Sanger sequencing and restriction fragment-length polymorphism analysis.
25. Observe the restoration of hairless phenotype in mice with exchanged wild-type exon 3.
26. Use flow cytometry to assess the recovery of CD3+ T lymphocytes in the peripheral blood of mice with exchanged exon 3.
27. Ensure that the repaired Foxn1 allele is conserved in the next generation.
1. Grow 293T and 293L cells in high-glucose DMEM supplemented with 8% bovine growth serum, 2 mM l-glutamine, 25 U/ml penicillin, and 25 μg/ml streptomycin.
2. Culture 293L cells harboring BAC16WT, BAC16 ORF59-Flag, or BAC16RTASTOP in DMEM with 50μg/mL hygromycin B.
3. Maintain iSLK.219, iSLKTet-RTABAC16WT, and iSLKTet-RTABAC16RTASTOP cells in DMEM with 10% Tet-Free Fetal Bovine Serum, 600μg/mL hygromycin B, 400μg/mL G418, and 1μg/mL puromycin.
4. Induce iSLK.219 cells with recombinant KSHV BACs using doxycycline.
5. Grow TRExBCBL1-RTA and BCBL-1 cells in RPMI supplemented with 8% fetal bovine serum, 2 mM l-glutamine, 25 U/ml penicillin, and 25 μg/ml streptomycin.
6. Select and maintain BCBL-1 cells transduced with shRNA PRMT5 lentiviral vectors on 1μg/mL puromycin.
7. Transduce BACmid-containing 293L cells with indicated lentiviral vectors and maintain on 1μg/mL puromycin.
8. Generate constitutively expressing ORF59-Flag and dsRedORF59-Flag in 293L cells using a lentivirus system.
9. Transfect 293T cells with pLVX-ORF59-Flag or pLVXdsRed-ORF59-Flag along with packaging vectors CMV-dR8.2 and pCMV-VSVG for virion production.
10. Add collected viruses to target cells for transduction and select with puromycin (2 mg/ml) to obtain a pure population.
11. Transfect BAC16 ORF59-Flag into 293L cells with Metafectene Pro followed by selection with hygromycin.
12. Monitor selection in both cell lines with GFP or RFP signals encoded by the lentivirus and the BACmid.
13. Incubate all cultures at 37°C in a humidified environment supplemented with 5% CO2.
14. Generate plasmids by PCR amplification and cloning into respective vectors.
15. Confirm the integrity of clones by sequencing at Nevada, Genomics Center, Reno.
16. Insert epitope tag at the C-terminus of ORF59 by homologous recombination using a two-step galK positive/counter selection scheme.
17. Electroporate PCR product into competent E. coli strain SW102 containing BAC16 and select mutants on chloramphenicol/kanamycin agar plates.
18. Confirm correct insertional mutants by restriction digestion with BamHI and Southern blot analysis.
19. Replace GalK-KanR cassette by electroporating a double stranded oligo and plating on 2-deoxy galactose containing agar plates for counter selection.
20. Screen correct colonies and confirm by southern blot analysis, PCR amplification of junctions, and sequence analysis.
21. Perform co-immunoprecipitations and Western blotting on transfected 293T cells.
22. Perform chromatin immunoprecipitation and purify DNA for qPCR amplification.
23. Conduct LowCell ChIP using the LowCell ChIP Kit and Bioruptor Pico.
24. Prepare DNA sequencing libraries for ChIP-seq and analyze using CLC Workbench 10.0.1.
25. Transfect iSLK.219 cells with SmartPool siRNA for control or PRMT5 using RNAiMax transfection procedure.
26. Transfect pGIPz shPRMT5 and pGIPzshControl vectors with packaging plasmids into 293Lenti-X T cells and induce with NaB.
27. Concentrate lentiviral particles by centrifugation and add to BCBL-1 cells treated with polybrene.
28. Select transduced cells with 1μg/mL puromycin and test knockdown efficiencies with Western blotting and comparative qPCR.
29. Perform KSHV transcriptome analysis on transfected and transduced 293L cell lines using real-time qPCR.
30. Purify GST proteins and perform in vitro translation for 35S-methionine labeled proteins.
31. Conduct in vitro binding assays and autoradiography with translated proteins and GST-fusion proteins.
32. Deposit ChIP-seq next generation sequence data to NCBI genbank with accession number Series GSE98058.
33. Analyze all data using Prism 6 software for significance.

steps.action: Dissect the required number of Drosophila larval brains in PBS after 48 h of larval hatching.
Fix the larval brains with 1% formaldehyde in PBS for 10 min at room temperature.
Quench the fixation with 125 mM glycine.
Dissociate and resuspend the larval brains according to the previously established method.
Sort the cells on BD FACSAria according to the strength of GFP and size of the NSCs to obtain a pure population of type II NSCs.
Culture K562 cells in RPMI medium supplemented with 10% Fetal Bovine Serum at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Fix K562 cells with 1% formaldehyde for 10 min at room temperature.
Quench the crosslink with 125 mM glycine.
Sort the K562 cells on BD FACSAria cell sorter using Hoechst stain and directly sort 100 cells in RIPA 140 mM.
Resuspend 1.2 million FACS sorted NSCs per replicate in 140 mM RIPA and subject to 14 cycles of sonication on a bioruptor with 30 secs 'ON'/'OFF' at high settings.
Centrifuge the sonicated samples at 14,000 g for 10 min at 4°C and transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube.
Incubate the extracts overnight with 2 μg of specific antibody at 4°C with head-over-tail rotations.
Add 20 μl of blocked Protein A and G Dynabeads to the tubes and incubate for 3 h to capture the antibodies.
Separate the beads with a magnetic rack and wash once with 140 mM RIPA, four times with 250 mM RIPA, and twice with TE buffer, pH 8.0.
Treat the immunoprecipitated samples with RNase and Proteinase K for reversal of cross-links, 12 h at 37°C and at least 6 h at 65°C.
Subject the samples to phenol–chloroform extraction after Proteinase K treatment.
Precipitate, pellet, and dissolve the DNA in 30 μl of TE buffer, pH 8.0.
Convert the recovered DNA into libraries using NebNext Ultra II DNA library preparation kit, following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Fix cells for TAF-ChIP with 1% formaldehyde in PBS for 10 min at room temperature and quench with 125 mM glycine for 5 min.
Wash the cells once with ice-cold PBS and directly sort in 240 μl of 140 mM RIPA.
Sonicate the sorted cells with three cycles at low power settings for breaking the nuclei.
Couple 15 μl of Protein A and G Dynabeads to 1 μg of specific antibody in blocking buffer for 2-3 h at 4°C.
Centrifuge the partially fragmented chromatin at 2,000 g for 10 min at 4°C and transfer the supernatant to the tube with blocked and antibody-coupled beads.
Incubate the samples at 4°C overnight with head-over-tail rotations.
Wash the samples twice briefly with 300 μl of homemade tagmentation buffer using a magnetic rack for beads separation.
Resuspend the washed beads in 20 μl of 1× tagmentation DNA buffer containing 1 μl of Nextera DNA tagmentation enzyme and incubate at 37°C for 40 min with constant shaking.
Wash the beads once with 140 mM RIPA, four times with 250 mM RIPA, and twice with TE buffer, pH 8.0.
Treat the samples with proteinase K in TE buffer overnight at 60°C with shaking.
Either perform phenol–chloroform extraction or directly PCR-amplify the samples after deactivating proteinase K.
Purify the PCR reaction with bead-based size selection to remove fragments larger than 1,000 bp.
Analyze the libraries on Agilent Bioanalyzer for size distribution and measure the concentration using a Qubit fluorometer.
Pool the finished libraries in equimolar amounts and sequence on Illumina NextSeq 500.
Use 2 μl of TAF and conventional ChIP library to check enrichment with various primer pairs on Applied Biosystem ViiA 7 real-time machine using SYBR green reagent.
Perform demultiplexing and fastq file conversion using blc2fastq.
Map reads from ChIP-Seq libraries using bowtie2 and filter for uniquely mapped reads.
Normalize the mapped BAM files to RPKMs using deepTools and generate bigwig coverage files.
Perform peak calling using MACS2 with specified settings for each sample type.
Annotate the resulting peaks with the ChIPseeker package using nearest gene to peak summit as assignment criteria.
Merge individual peaks of corresponding modification and approach using bedTools.
Calculate the overlaps with ChIPpeakAnno package using specified commands for each sample type.
Submit all the ChIP-Seq data generated in the study to the GEO database (GSE112633).

steps: 1. Screen publicly available datasets for Arabidopsis genes of unknown function that exhibit transcriptional signatures of CBGs or CCGs.
2. Identify At2g35260 as a gene of interest and designate it BCM1.
3. Perform immunoblot analyses using BCM1 antiserum raised against recombinant Arabidopsis His-BCM155 to detect BCM1 protein accumulation in various Arabidopsis tissues.
4. Observe BCM1 expression patterns and compare them to key CBGs such as GUN4.
5. Analyze BCM1 protein levels in young and mature rosette leaves, during senescence, and in etiolated seedlings before and after illumination.
6. Determine the amino acid sequence of BCM1, noting the presence of an N-terminal chloroplast transit peptide (cTP) and six transmembrane domains (TMDs).
7. Transiently express BCM1 fused to yellow fluorescent protein (YFP) in Arabidopsis protoplasts and confirm chloroplast localization.
8. Isolate envelope, stroma, and thylakoid fractions of chloroplasts and perform immunoblot analysis to determine BCM1 distribution.
9. Treat isolated thylakoids with chaotropic and alkaline reagents to assess whether BCM1 is an integral or peripheral thylakoid protein.
10. Characterize the status of TBS in bcm1 mutants and BCM1-overexpressing (BCM1-OX) plants.
11. Identify three allelic Arabidopsis bcm1-null mutants and observe their phenotypes under standard growth conditions and various light-stress regimes.
12. Measure ALA synthesis rates in bcm1 mutants and BCM1-OX plants.
13. Supplement bcm1 mutants with ALA and assess the impact on the pale-green leaf phenotype.
14. Quantify Proto, Mg-porphyrins, Chl, and non-covalently bound heme levels in bcm1 mutants and BCM1-OX plants.
15. Examine the expression of CBGs and steady-state levels of CBEs in bcm1 and BCM1-OX seedlings using immunoblot analyses.
16. Perform quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) analyses to measure transcripts of all CBGs in bcm1 and BCM1-OX seedlings.
17. Investigate the genetic interaction between BCM1 and MgCh by generating bcm1-3 gun5 and bcm1-3 gun4 double mutants.
18. Cross BCM1-OX plants with gun5-1 and two gun4 mutants to study epistatic relationships.
19. Conduct a yeast two-hybrid (Y2H) screen to identify potential BCM1 interaction partners in the TBS pathway.
20. Confirm BCM1 interactions with GluTR, GUN4, and CHLM using bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC).
21. Isolate thylakoid membranes from bcm1-3 gun4-1 and BCM1-OX3/gun4-1 seedlings and perform in vitro MgCh activity assays with and without recombinant His-GUN4.
22. Express His-BCM1 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae cell membranes and conduct MgCh assays using isolated yeast membranes.
23. Analyze the effect of purified His-BCM1 on MgCh activity in vitro, considering the impact of non-ionic detergents on the assay.
24. Investigate the contributions of BCM1 and BCM2 to Chl biosynthesis using bcm2 T-DNA insertion knockdown mutants and the bcm1-3 bcm2-2 double mutant.
25. Perform virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) of BCM2 in WT and bcm1-3 plants.
26. Generate bcm1-2 complementation lines that constitutively express BCM2 driven by the 35S promoter (BCM2-OX/bcm1).
27. Determine Chl degradation rates in detached leaves from WT, bcm1, BCM1-OX, bcm1-3 bcm2-2, BCM1-OX9, and BCM2-OX1/bcm1 seedlings subjected to dark-induced senescence (DIS).
28. Conduct electron microscopic analyses of chloroplast structure during DIS.
29. Perform a Y2H analysis to study interactions between BCMs and Chl catabolic enzymes (CCEs).
30. Confirm BCM interactions with SGR1 using BiFC and co-immunoprecipitation assays.
31. Transiently overexpress SGR1 and BCMs in tobacco leaves to test the impact on Chl breakdown and SGR1 stability.
32. Cross BCM1-OX plants with SGR1-overexpressing (SGR1-OX) lines to confirm the effect on Chl levels and SGR1 accumulation in Arabidopsis.
1. Obtain approval from the UCSF Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee and adhere to the Office of Laboratory Animal Welfare guidelines.
2. Use mouse strains C57BL/6, Tlr7−/−, Tlr9−/−, Myd88−/−, and Tlr7−/−Tlr9−/− double knockout mice, ensuring a C57BL/6 background of greater than 95% by microsatellite genotyping.
3. Maintain P. berghei strain ANKA parasites in C57BL/6 mice, sourced from the MR4 stock centre.
4. On day 5 of infection, harvest blood from an infected mouse via cardiac puncture.
5. Introduce 10^6 infected erythrocytes into a new mouse by intraperitoneal injection in 100 μl of Alsever’s solution, initiating all infections at 14.00 hours.
6. For cytokine analysis, harvest blood by submandibular blood collection or cardiac puncture into K2EDTA for plasma isolation.
7. Monitor survival and signs of cerebral malaria daily, and twice daily during the peak of lethality (days 6 through 12).
8. Consider animals with neurological symptoms or those that die on or before day 12 post-infection as having cerebral malaria.
9. Monitor parasitaemia daily by Giemsa-stained thin film blood smears.
10. Assess the significance of parasitaemia courses using the Mann–Whitney U test (α = 0.05).
11. Assess the significance of survival courses by comparing Kaplan-Meier curves using the log rank (Mantel-Cox) test (α = 0.05).
12. Measure all plasma cytokines by multiplexed cytometric bead immunoassay (Millipore) following the manufacturer's instructions.
13. Detect cytokines on a MAGPIX (Luminex) system.
14. Assess cytokine level significance using a Mann–Whitney U test (α = 0.05).

steps.action: Treat satellite cells associated with myofibers with tibialis anterior (TA) muscle extracts.
Maintain control myofibers in Dulbecco's modified Eagle medium (DMEM) alone.
Perform immunofluorescence studies to assess the proportions of PAX7+, MYOD+, PAX7+, Ki67+, and PAX7+, EdU+ satellite cells after 24 hours in floating culture condition.
Isolate healthy intact myofibers from extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscles.
Mechanically damage isolated myofibers with a Pasteur pipette in a culture dish and confirm damage based on shrunken morphology.
Co-culture intact myofibers with damaged myofibers and perform immunofluorescence analysis at 48 and 72 hours of culture.
Wash out damaged myofibers and culture media containing DMDFs and replace with fresh DMEM.
Culture for an additional 24 hours and perform further immunofluorescence analysis.
Evaluate cell size of satellite cells stimulated by damaged myofibers.
Perform proteome analysis with biological replicates to identify DMDFs.
Screen proteins ranging from 10 to 50 kDa on SDS-PAGE gels.
Treat isolated myofibers associated with satellite cells with recombinant proteins of AK-1, CK, GAPDH, PGAM-2, and TPI in floating culture condition for 72 hours.
Immunostain treated myofibers for MYOD and PAX7.
Treat satellite cells associated with myofibers with metabolic enzymes in a non-glucose medium.
Test the necessity of HGF signaling for satellite cell activation induced by DMDFs using a c-MET inhibitor.
Test the involvement of major signaling pathways in DMDF-induced entry of satellite cells into the G1 phase using various inhibitors.
Pre-expose satellite cells associated with myofibers to recombinant enzyme proteins for 48 hours under floating culture conditions.
Stimulate pre-exposed satellite cells with growth-factor-rich medium (GM) for an additional 24 hours.
Administer GAPDH recombinant protein into TA muscles 24 hours prior to injection of BaCl2 to induce muscle regeneration.
Use PBS as a control for in vivo experiments.
Perform qPCR analysis to measure the expression of Pax7 and MyoD genes.
Conduct immunohistochemistry to assess the number of PAX7+ EdU+ proliferative satellite cells in regenerating muscles.
Obtain ethical approval for the study (Leeds East REC 06/Q1206/180).
Perform laser micro-dissection (LMD) on formalin-fixed/paraffin-embedded tissue using a Zeiss/PALM Microscope as per the Supplementary materials and methods.
Define and select CAFs and NFs based on their proximity to tumor masses or normal epithelium, ensuring areas selected are devoid of other visible cell types.
Perform SMA staining using a mouse monoclonal antibody (M851, Dako) at a dilution of 1:1000 with an IntelliPATH automated stainer following the manufacturer's standard conditions.
Obtain MCF7 and HB2 cells from the European Collection of Cell Cultures.
Confer stable GFP expression to cells using the pTH-GFPa selectable GFP expression vector.
Obtain MCF7 cells that stably express firefly luciferase from Cell Biolabs (#AKR-234).
Isolate primary fibroblasts from breast surgical samples and immortalize them by hTERT retroviral transduction as previously described.
Perform reverse transfection of pre-/anti-miR and/or plasmids using HiPerFect (Qiagen).
Perform stable miR-26b/control 'knock-down' using pmiRZIP lentiviral vectors (System Biosciences).
Carry out assays for cell viability, cell cycle, apoptosis, migration, and invasion as previously described.
Perform flow-cytometry and fluorescence-activated cell sorting on LSRII (BD Biosciences) and MoFlo (Dako) machines, respectively.
Carry out spheroid invasion assays with modifications of a previously described method.
Formalin-fix/paraffin-embed spheroids, cut 5 µm sections, and stain with haematoxylin/eosin or treat for immunohistochemistry with rabbit anti-cytokeratin (Ab9377, Abcam).
Use dual luciferase assays and pmiRGLO reporter (Promega) as described in the Supplementary materials and methods.
Extract RNA from FFPE using RecoverAll Total Nucleic Acid Isolation (Ambion).
Extract miRNA and mRNA from cell lines using MirVana miRNA Isolation (Ambion) and RNeasy (Qiagen), respectively.
Perform qPCR analyses on 7500/7900HT machines in triplicate with Taqman assays (Life Technologies).
Conduct microarray analyses of miRNA expression using human miRNA v2 arrays and system v1.7 reagents (Agilent).

Separate peptides from processed lysates of cell pellets by capillary liquid chromatography (LC) and analyze by tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) using the RSLCnano system and LTQ-Orbitrap Velos mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific).
Perform data search against the IPI Human 3.87 database and label-free quantitation (LFQ) using MaxQuant 1.2.2.5.
Perform statistical analyses using Prism (GraphPad) with two-tailed tests as described in the text.
Analyze mass spectrometry data using R, log2 median-normalize expression levels, perform t-tests, and convert p-values to false discovery rates using Benjamini–Hochberg methodology.

steps: Compile a database with protein sequences of 93 vertebrate TDP43 homologs.
Split the database into separate collections of NTDs, RRM domains, and CTDs.
Calculate the Levenshtein or edit distance normalized to a sequence length of 100 amino acids between all members of each category.
Analyze the amino-acid composition of the CR and each of the two IDRs that bracket the CR.
Calculate the hydrophobicity throughout the human TDP43 CTD in a sliding window of five amino acids using fourteen different hydrophobicity scales.
Apply the hydrophobicity analysis to the entire set of vertebrate TDP43 CTDs to assess periodicity and amplitude.
Replace the RNA-binding RRM domains of TDP43 with GFP to generate a reporter protein (TDP43 RRM-GFP).
Use the TDP43 RRM-GFP reporter assay to screen a panel of CTD mutants with systematic alterations in the composition and spacing of selected hydrophobic motifs or residues.
Introduce mutations identified by the reporter assay into the context of full-length TDP43 to study their effect on splicing.
Combine high-throughput automated confocal microscopy and flow cytometry to monitor nuclear and total GFP fluorescence in cells expressing TDP43 RRM-GFP with WT or mutant IDRs.
Estimate the critical concentration required for phase separation (Csat) of WT TDP43 RRM-GFP.
Purify full-length TDP43 with WT, F-S, or FYW-S variant CTDs from bacteria.
Investigate the phase separation behavior of purified full-length TDP43 variants in vitro.
Test the effect of RNA on the phase separation of purified WT and mutant TDP43.
Use live-cell reporter assay to decode the interactions that determine the material properties of TDP43 condensates.
Assess material properties of TDP43 RRM-GFP droplets using half-bleach FRAP experiments.
Design mutants to reduce the number of hydrophobic clusters in the TDP43 CTD and test their effects on droplet dynamics and morphology.
Predict the effect of ALS-associated and engineered IDR mutations on the phase properties of TDP43 RRM-GFP droplets.
Rationally design second-site suppressor mutations to rescue or restore altered phase dynamics produced by primary mutations.
Build a flow cytometry-compatible splicing reporter to co-express a splicing-sensitive fluorescent protein and full-length TDP43 (or variants) from the same transiently transfected plasmid.
Establish the dependency of splicing on TDP43 by transfecting the splicing reporter into WT and TDP43−/− HEK-293T cells.
Co-express the splicing module in TDP43−/− cells with full-length TDP43 CTD mutants fused to an N-terminal BFP tag.
Normalize the efficiency of TDP43-mediated exon skipping to the expression level of the splicing reporter and plot against the total expression levels of re-introduced TDP43.
Re-introduce GFP-tagged, full-length TDP43 variants into TDP43−/− HEK-293T cells by stable transduction.
Estimate the nuclear TDP43 concentrations in the add-back lines.
Select previously validated endogenous targets containing cryptic exons suppressed by TDP43 for analysis.
Analyze the endogenous mRNAs expressed from these genes by RT-PCR for the presence of the relevant cryptic exons.

steps.description: Design cDNAs from published protein sequences and clone into pBABED-Puro vectors for constitutive expression.
Verify all DNA constructs by DNA sequencing using Applied Biosystems Big-Dye v. 3.1 chemistry on an Applied Biosystems model 3730 automated capillary DNA sequencer.

Culture human U2OS osteosarcoma, A549 pulmonary adenocarcinoma cells, mouse J774 monocyte, human MDA-MB-468 mammary gland adenocarcinoma, MDA-MB-231 breast cancer and K-562 erythroleukaemia cells in their respective media supplemented with 10% FBS, 2 mM L-glutamine, and 1% penicillin/streptomycin at 37°C in a humidified incubator at 5% CO2.
For retroviral production, co-transfect pBABED retroviral plasmids with pCMV-gag-pol and pCMV-VSV-G in 293-FT cells and collect retroviruses 24 h post-transfection.
Infect target cells with retroviral medium containing polybrene and select with puromycin.
Wash cells twice in ice-cold PBS, scrape in lysis buffer with protease inhibitors and β-mercaptoethanol, clarify cell extracts and determine protein concentration using Bradford protein assay.
Incubate lysates with anti-FLAG M2 resin, wash, and elute FLAG-fusion proteins with SDS sample buffer for SDS-PAGE.
Reconstitute EGF in sterile PBS and stimulate serum-deprived cells with EGF.
Reconstitute Imatinib mesylate in DMSO and incubate cells with Imatinib in serum-free DMEM prior to lysis.
Reconstitute SHP099 and MLN4924 in DMSO and incubate cells with these inhibitors in serum-free DMEM prior to lysis.
Separate proteins on SDS-PAGE gels, transfer to PVDF or nitrocellulose membranes, block, incubate with primary and secondary antibodies, wash, and detect with ECL reagent.
Wash cells in PBS, harvest, isolate RNA, synthesize cDNA, and perform RT-PCR with specific primers.
Transfect cells with siRNA oligonucleotides using Lipofectamine RNAiMAX, replace transfection medium with fresh growth medium after 16 h, and lyse cells at specified time points.

steps: 1. Isolate mRNAs from adult heads of TBPH-null alleles (tbphΔ23 and tbphΔ142) and wild-type controls.
2. Hybridize the isolated mRNAs to GeneChip Drosophila Genome 2.0 Arrays.
3. Perform statistical analysis to identify dysregulated transposons in TBPH-minus alleles compared to wild type.
