4. Independently confirm microarray modifications using quantitative RT-PCR (qRT-PCR) with primers against RNA sequences transcribed from dysregulated transposons.
5. Detect the upregulation of the glycoprotein env, codified by gypsy, in TBPH-minus heads using qRT-PCR or other methodologies.
6. Test the repression of accord and gypsy activation by genetic expression of the TBPH protein in TBPH-mutant backgrounds.
7. Treat TBPH-null flies with nucleoside and non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs and NNRTIs) to assess the effect on locomotive defects.
8. Silence the expression of gypsy in tbphΔ23 homozygous flies using transgenic flies carrying RNAi constructs against gypsy (gypsy-IR) cloned in UAS expression vectors.
9. Express the RNAi constructs against gypsy using pan-neuronal driver elav-GAL4 or motoneuronal promoter D42-GAL4 and assess the locomotive phenotypes.
10. Analyze the effect of gypsy suppression on the growth of presynaptic terminals and the formation of glutamate receptor clusters at the postsynaptic membranes.
11. Test the suppression of gypsy in glial cells using repo-GAL4 and evaluate the impact on locomotive phenotypes.
12. Utilize a GFP-IR construct co-expressed with a GFP reporter in transgenic flies to assess the efficiency of the RNA silencing machinery in different genetic backgrounds.

13. Use qRT-PCR to measure the brain levels of the principal constituents of the RISC complex (Dicer-2, loquacious, Argonaute 2) and other genes associated with the silencing of LTR (piwi, pasha, homeless) in TBPH-mutant heads.
14. Compare the protein levels of Dcr-2 in mutant fly heads to controls.
15. Suppress TDP-43 in human neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y cells and measure the expression levels of the human Dicer protein.
16. Express a FLAG-tagged isoform of TBPH in Drosophila neurons and perform pull-down assays from fly head tissues to test for physical interaction with Dcr-2 mRNA.
17. Assess the interaction between TBPH and Dcr-2 at the protein level to determine if they form part of the same protein complex in neurons.

18. Recover the expression levels of Dcr-2 in TBPH-mutant backgrounds by crossing transgenic flies containing UAS-Dcr-2 with flies carrying pan-neuronal driver elav-GAL4 or motoneuron promoter D42-GAL4.
19. Evaluate the effect of UAS-Dcr-2 expression in neurons or motoneurons on the locomotive problems of TBPH-null larvae.
20. Observe the impact of UAS-Dcr-2 expression on the outgrowth of motoneuron synaptic terminals and muscle innervation.
21. Assess the reorganization of glutamate receptor clusters at the postsynaptic membranes following UAS-Dcr-2 expression.
22. Determine if UAS-Dcr-2 expression can prevent the augmented expression of gypsy in TBPH-mutant brains.
23. Express Dcr-2 in glial cells using repo-GAL4 and evaluate the rescue of locomotive deficiencies in TBPH-minus flies.
24. Analyze the effect of Dcr-2 expression in glial cells on the wrapping of motoneuron axons and the non-autonomous growth of neuromuscular synapses.
25. Treat TBPH-minus larvae with enoxacin and assess recovery of locomotive capacities and motoneuron innervation patterns.
1. House male albino Wistar rats (250 to 270 g) at a constant room temperature of 22°C ± 1°C and 60% relative humidity on a 12:12-hour light–dark cycle with free access to food and water.
2. Anesthetize rats with chloral hydrate (400 mg/kg) and position them in a stereotaxic apparatus.
3. Perform injections into the substantia nigra (SN) at coordinates 5.5 mm posterior, 1.8 mm lateral, and 8.3 mm ventral to the bregma, 2 hours after the first stressor application.
4. Establish five groups of animals for different treatments: V (vehicle/nonstressed control), S (vehicle/stressed), L (LPS/nonstressed), SL (LPS/stressed), and SLR (LPS/stressed/RU486).
5. Administer a single intranigral injection of 2 μl of vehicle or LPS as appropriate for each group.
6. Subject the stressed groups to a 9-day variate stressor paradigm, with stress application times varying between 08:00 and 20:00.
7. For restraint stress, place each animal in a 21 cm × 6 cm plastic tube with plaster tape on the outside and a 6-cm hole at the far end for breathing.
8. For forced swimming stress, place the animal in a glass tank with 22 cm of water at 23°C ± 2°C.
9. Measure body weight at the beginning and end of the 10-day treatment.
10. Deeply anesthetize rats and collect blood from the heart for serum corticosterone measurement using ELISA.
11. Perform immunohistological evaluation on thaw-mounted 20-μm coronal sections cut on a cryostat at -15°C and mounted on gelatine-coated slides.
12. Incubate sections with primary antibodies against tyrosine hydroxylase, glial fibrillary acidic protein, Iba-1, and OX-6 in Tris-buffered saline (TBS), pH 7.4.
13. Treat sections with 0.3% hydrogen peroxide in methanol for 20 minutes, wash, and incubate in TBS with 1% horse or goat serum for 60 minutes in a humidity chamber.
14. Incubate sections with biotinylated secondary antibodies and then with ExtrAvidin–Peroxidase buffered aqueous solution.
15. Visualize peroxidase using a standard diaminobenzidine–hydrogen peroxide reaction for 5 minutes.
16. Analyze immunohistochemical data in a bounded region of the SN and estimate the number of neurons using a fractionator sampling design.

17. Perform immunofluorescence staining on sections, block with serum, incubate with primary antibodies, followed by fluorescently labeled secondary antibodies, and counterstain nuclei with Hoechst dye.
18. Acquire fluorescence images using a confocal laser scanning microscope and process with associated software.
19. Dissect the left SN 6 hours after injection, snap-freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at -80°C.
20. Extract total RNA from the SN using the RNeasy kit and synthesize cDNA using the QuantiTect Reverse Transcription Kit.
21. Perform real-time PCR with iQ SYBR Green Supermix, primers, and cDNA, followed by melting curve analysis.
22. Lyse SN in buffer, centrifuge the homogenate, estimate protein content, and perform Western blot analysis using anti-Cox-2 and β-actin antibodies.
23. Determine lipid hydroperoxide levels using the FOX assay adapted for a microplate reader.
24. Express results as mean ± SD and perform statistical analysis using Student’s t-test or ANOVA followed by LSD test for post hoc comparisons.

steps.action: Obtain Arabidopsis accessions from the Nottingham Arabidopsis Stock Centre and other specified sources.
Generate a construct for expressing HaRxL62 by recombining the ORF into pENTR/SD/D-TOPO, then into pENS-StrepII-3×HA-GW.
Transform Arabidopsis Col-0 with the construct using Agrobacterium tumefaciens strain GV3101 and the floral dipping method.
Select primary transformants (T1) on soil containing BASTA and check for HaRxL62 expression by Western blot analysis.
Observe T2 progeny for 3:1 segregation and select homozygous lines by examining BASTA resistance of T3 seedlings.
Grow Arabidopsis plants for Hpa-inoculation assay at 22°C, 60% humidity, under a 10-h photoperiod and 14-h dark period in growth cabinets.
Grow Arabidopsis plants for SA-induced PR1 expression analysis on 0.7% agar MS medium plates at 22°C, under a 16-h photoperiod and 8-h dark period in growth cabinets.
Spray-inoculate Arabidopsis plants with a spore suspension of Hpa to saturation and maintain under high humidity conditions at 16°C until sampling.
Stain leaves inoculated with Hpa with trypan blue to evaluate hyphae growth and HR cell death.
Harvest 5 pools of 3 plants each, vortex in water, and determine conidiospore amount using a haemocytometer.
Extract total RNA using TRI reagent and 1-bromo-3-chloropropane, precipitate with isopropanol and high salt buffer, treat with DNaseI, and purify with RNeasy Mini Kit.
Generate cDNAs from total RNA using Invitrogen Superscript II Reverse Transcriptase protocol, dilute, and use for qPCR.
Perform qPCR with SYBR Green mix, diluted cDNAs, and primers, using a thermal cycler and calculate relative expression values.
Extract genomic DNA from Hpa Waco9 conidiospores using Nucleon PhytoPure DNA extraction kit.
Prepare a paired-end library, sequence on Illumina Genome Analyzer II, and align reads to Hpa Emoy2 v8.3 genome.
Correct Hpa genome by substituting Waco9 SNVs using a custom Perl script and deposit sequence data in NCBI's SRA.
Perform RNA sequencing, shear double stranded cDNAs, sequence libraries, align reads to genomes, and analyze differential expression.
Identify cis-regulatory elements by extracting sequences upstream of start codons, analyze with MEME, FIMO, and TOMTOM, and compare against databases.
Conduct GO enrichment analysis using AgriGO with FDR=0.05 for Arabidopsis genes categorized into four groups.
Assay GUS activity histochemically, vacuum-infiltrate leaves with staining solution, incubate, destain, and observe under a microscope.
Perform SA-induced PR1 expression analysis on ten-day-old plants, incubate with SA, dry, flash-freeze, and extract RNA.

steps: 1. Identify a dominant CD4+ T cell epitope in the nucleocapsid (N) protein of SARS-CoV (N353) recognized in BALB/c mice.
2. Evaluate intranasal (i.n.) immunization versus footpad vaccination for generating local versus systemic T cell responses.
3. Vaccinate BALB/c mice twice at 6–7 week intervals with VRP-SARS-N or a control VRP expressing green fluorescent protein (VRP-GFP) i.n. or subcutaneously (s.c.) prior to challenge.
4. Assess the induction of N-specific CD4+ T cell responses in the lungs, airways, and spleen following vaccination.
5. Challenge vaccinated mice with mouse-adapted SARS-CoV and evaluate protection from lethal disease.
6. Deplete memory CD4+ T cells systemically 2 days prior to challenge to assess their role in protection.
7. Treat vaccinated mice with CD4+ T-cell-depleting antibody 98 days prior to challenge to confirm the importance of memory CD4+ T cells.
8. Analyze histological changes and virus clearance kinetics in immunized mice after challenge.
9. Use a modified method to label cells by i.v. and i.n. administration of CD90.2 and CD45 antibodies to discriminate between cells localized to the airway versus parenchyma and vasculature.
10. Examine the phenotype and effector function of airway, parenchymal, and vascular N353 memory CD4+ T cells.
11. Treat infected mice with FTY720 to prevent T cell egress from lymphoid tissue and then treat with BrdU to assess local proliferation or recruitment of N353 CD4+ T cells.
12. Deplete CD4+ T cells in the airways by i.n. administration of anti-CD4+ T cell antibody prior to challenge to explicitly address the role of airway cells in protection.
13. Measure IFN-γ mRNA levels in the lungs of VRP-SARS-N-immunized mice after challenge.
14. Use an in vivo cytokine expression assay with Brefeldin A (BFA) treatment to confirm IFN-γ expression by CD4+ T cells.
15. Neutralize IFN-γ in the airway by i.n. administration prior to infection and every 2 days thereafter to study its role in gene upregulation.
16. Assess the effect of airway IFN-γ neutralization on mortality, pathological changes in the lungs, and virus clearance kinetics.
17. Administer IFN-γ (but not TNF) in the airway to test its protective effect after SARS-CoV challenge.
18. Investigate the role of airway memory CD4+ T cells in respiratory dendritic cell (rDC) migration to mediastinal lymph nodes (MLNs) and in enhancing the adaptive immune response.
19. Assess the effect of airway memory CD4+ T cells and IFN-γ on the migration and maturation of rDCs to MLNs.
20. Evaluate the role of airway CD4+ T-cell-derived IFN-γ in promoting CXCR3-dependent CD8+ T cell mobilization to the infected lung.
21. Block CXCR3 systemically to confirm its importance in CD8+ T cell accumulation in the lungs.
22. Induce IL-10 expression by SARS-N353-specific CD4+ T cells in the lung after direct ex vivo or in vivo stimulation and assess its role in protection.
23. Block the IL-10 receptor to study the contribution of IL-10 to survival and virus clearance.
24. Compare eosinophil infiltration into the lungs of VRP-SARS-N immunized mice to control VRP-immunized mice after challenge.
25. Examine N proteins from various coronaviruses for a SARS-N353 epitope-like sequence.
26. Challenge hDPP4-expressing mice with MERS-CoV and detect MERS-N350-specific CD4+ T cells.
27. Immunize mice with VRP-MERS-N and boost to generate a robust airway CD4+ T cell response.
28. Analyze the effector function of these cells and their impact on virus clearance upon challenge.
29. Immunize HLA class II DR2 or DR3 transgenic mice with N peptides and analyze for peptide-specific CD4+ T cell responses.
30. Challenge HLA transgenic mice with SARS-CoV or MERS-CoV after immunization and measure virus clearance kinetics.
31. Assess cross-reactivity of memory CD4+ T cells induced by VRP-MERS-N against peptides from various coronaviruses.
32. Evaluate the protective effect of VRP-MERS-N-induced cross-reactive memory CD4+ T cells against SARS-CoV challenge.
33. Immunize with VRP-HKU4-N to induce cross-reactive CD4+ T cell responses and assess MERS-CoV clearance after challenge.

steps.description: Maintain C. elegans animals using standard culture conditions at 25°C.
Synchronize animals through alkaline hypochlorite treatment of gravid adults to isolate eggs.
Use SapTrap to construct the 30xlinker::GFP^SEC^TEV::AID degron::3xFLAG repair template (pJW1747) for generating the knock-in into the 3′ end of the nhr-25 gene.
Generate DH10β competent E. coli cells in-house for plasmid production.
Assemble the final repair template using pDD379, annealed oligos 3482+3483, pJW1779, 3′ homology arm PCR product, pJW1347, pDD372, pDD363, and pJW1759.
Purify the pJW1747 repair template using the Invitrogen PureLink HQ Mini Plasmid DNA Purification Kit with an optional wash step using a 4 M guanidine-HCl + 40% isopropanol solution.
Inject N2 animals with a mix of 10 ng/µL pJW1747, 50 ng/µL pDD121, and co-injection markers (10 ng/µL pGH8, 5 ng/µL pCFJ104, 2.5 ng/µL pCFJ90).
Isolate knock-ins and verify each knock-in junction via PCR using primers outside the homology arm and within pJW1747.
Backcross the knock-in five times against wild-type N2 animals to produce JDW58.
Excise the SEC from JDW58 by heat-shock to produce JDW59.
Re-confirm the knock-in sequence of JDW59 by PCR amplification and sequencing using oligos flanking the homology arms.
Cross JDW58 to CA1200 to generate JDW70.
Excise the SEC from JDW70 to produce JDW71.
Transfer synchronized L1 larval stage animals to standard NGM agar plates seeded with E. coli OP50.
Transfer animals at the P6.p 2-cell stage (mid-L3 stage) to OP50-seeded NGM agar plates treated with IAA, NAA, or K-NAA, or to M9 buffer containing NAA with or without bacteria.
Prepare a 250 mM stock solution of IAA or NAA in 95% ethanol and store at -20°C.
Dilute IAA or NAA into NGM agar at the time of pouring plates.
Seed plates with fresh OP50.
For K-NAA experiments, prepare a 250 mM stock solution in deionized water and store at 4°C.
Prepare a fresh 1 mM or 4 mM NAA solution in M9 buffer for experiments in M9 buffer.
Use M9 buffer alone as a control for NAA experiments in M9 buffer.
For microfluidic platform experiments, prepare a fresh solution of 4 mM NAA or K-NAA in M9 buffer containing E. coli NA22 and store at 4°C for up to 2 weeks.
Pick L4 hermaphrodites onto individual MYOB plates with varying ethanol and auxin concentrations and transfer to new plates daily over 4 days.
Count eggs laid on each plate after removing the parent and quantify viable progeny when F1 reaches L4 or adult stages.
Score for dead eggs and calculate brood size and percent embryonic lethality.
Construct RNAi targeting cul-1 by cloning synthetic DNA into the T444T RNAi vector.
Obtain RNAi feeding strains silencing skr-1/2, skr-7, skr-10, and rbx-1 from the Vidal RNAi library.
Plate synchronized L1 stage eft-3 > TIR1::mRuby; nhr-25::GFP::AID animals onto OP50 NGM agar plates with control or 4 mM NAA and grow for 24 hr at 25°C until early L3 stage.
Acquire images to score for the presence or absence of an AC using DIC optics.
Wash animals off plates with M9 and transfer onto plates with control or 4 mM NAA, then grow at 25°C until mid-L3 stage.
Acquire images to score for P6.p divisions using DIC optics and score for plate level adult phenotypes approximately 24 hr later.
Anesthetize animals on 5% agarose pads containing 10 mM sodium azide and secure with a coverslip for imaging.
Acquire images using a spinning disk confocal microscope or a microfluidic device with appropriate optics and cameras.
Process all acquired images using Fiji software.
Quantify AID::GFP degradation by measuring mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) and normalizing data.
Perform statistical analysis using Student’s t-test or Mann Whitney U-test to determine significance.
Compile figures using Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator.
Make data available upon reasonable request and deposit supplemental material at figshare.

steps: 1. Construct pCasRed plasmid carrying chloramphenicol resistance gene (CmR), Cas9 nuclease, λ Red (Exo, Beta, Gam) cassette, and tracrRNA.
2. Construct pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmid by fusing the kanamycin resistance gene (KmR) with the sacB gene and inserting the synthetic DNA fragment (gDNA) encoding the RNA guide.
3. Select gDNAs for target genes using bioinformatics tools like BLAST, ensuring no homology with other chromosomal regions.
4. Clone synthetic gDNAs between the two tracrRNA-complementary repeat regions in the pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmid.
5. Transform E. coli BL21(DE3)ΔompA(pCasRed) with the pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmids and select colonies on LB plates supplemented with Cm and Km.
6. Analyze transformation efficiencies and compare with the efficiency of the 'empty' pCRISPR vector to assess gDNA quality.
7. Randomly analyze ten clones from transformations using PCR and sequence analyses to verify the presence of the desired mutations.
8. Investigate the efficiency of gene inactivation using synthetic oligonucleotides (dDNA) under different conditions, focusing on length, concentration, and extent of deletion.
9. Design donor DNAs with homology arms of equal length upstream and downstream from the deletion.
10. Validate the best conditions for gene inactivation by targeting additional gene loci with single stranded or double stranded donor DNAs.
11. Analyze mutation efficiencies by examining at least 20 colonies from at least three independent experiments.
12. Construct pCRISPR-SacB-gDNAs plasmids for additional 'dispensable' genes according to the Keio library.
13. Verify the effectiveness of cloned gDNAs by transformation and colony counting.
14. Design 70 bp-ss-dDNAs to delete 30 bp and introduce a premature stop codon in each gene.

15. Transform E. coli BL21(DE3)ΔompA(pCasRed) with the corresponding pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmid and dDNA, and select colonies with transformation efficiencies between 2 and 5 × 10^2 CFUs/μg of plasmid DNA.
16. Randomly select ten colonies from each transformation and analyze by PCR for the presence of the 30 bp deletion.
17. Apply the 'ten colony rule' to establish the success rate of mutagenesis.
18. Attempt to rescue missing mutants by using dDNAs targeting the opposite strands.
19. Re-attempt the deletion of genes using double stranded dDNAs if ss-dDNAs fail.
20. Test the compatibility of mutations with the genetic background of the recipient strain by attempting deletions in BL21(DE3) wild type strain.
21. Create multi-gene mutants in a stepwise approach by removing the pCRISPR-gDNA plasmid after each knockout.
22. Grow mutant colonies in LB supplemented with Cm and 5% sucrose to eliminate the pCRISPR-SacB plasmid.
23. Prepare competent cells directly from the overnight culture for the subsequent mutagenesis step.
24. Co-transform E. coli BL21(DE3)ΔompA(pCasRed) with the next pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmid and the corresponding dDNA to target another gene locus.
25. Create pCRISPR plasmids carrying two gDNAs for simultaneous mutations at two separated genome loci.
26. Co-transform E. coli BL21(DE3)ΔompA(pCasRed) with the pCRISPR(gDNA)2 plasmid and two mutagenic oligonucleotides designed to repair and mutagenize the genome at the two cleaved sites.
27. Verify the simultaneous Cas-mediated cleavage at two chromosomal sites by analyzing colonies after co-transformation.

steps.description: Provide control and PLX5622 chows to C57BL/6J male mice, ensuring an intake of approximately 1.2 mg of PLX5622 per mouse per day.
Treat 8-week-old C57BL/6J mice with PLX5622 or control chow for 21 days.
Begin cranial irradiation 7 days after initiating drug treatment.
Anesthetize mice with intraperitoneal injection of ketamine (100 mg/kg) and xylazine (10 mg/kg).
Place anesthetized mice 16.3 cm from a cesium-137 source, shield eyes and body, and deliver 1.65 Gy of irradiation on both sides of the head every other day over 5 days for a total dose of 10 Gy.
House mice used for the NOR test in a room with reversed light cycle for at least 2 weeks before testing.
Handle mice for 5 minutes each day for 5 days prior to the NOR test.
Place mice in an open arena and allow them to explore for 10 minutes for two consecutive days.
Introduce two identical objects in the arena and let mice explore for 5 minutes on day 3.
Replace one object with a novel object and allow mice to explore for 5 minutes on day 4.
Record trials and analyze exploratory behavior using an overhead camera and video tracking system.
Perform the DMP dry maze test with four trials per day, guiding mice to the escape hole if necessary, and clean the maze with 70% ethanol after each trial.
Conduct the metric distance test over two consecutive days, with one habituation phase and three trials each day, altering the distance between objects.
Euthanize mice used for flow cytometry and perfuse with ice-cold PBS.
Dissociate brain samples using a Neural Tissue Dissociation Kit and perform a Percoll gradient separation.
Stain dissociated cells with fluorophore-conjugated antibodies and analyze using flow cytometry.
Euthanize mice used for Golgi staining at the end of the first NOR test, perfuse with ice-cold PBS, and process the right hemispheres for Golgi staining.
Immerse brain hemispheres in Golgi staining solution for 14 days, transfer to 30% sucrose, and store at 4°C.
Cut brains into 100 μm sections, mount on slides, and develop with Golgi-Cox staining solution.
Capture images of hippocampal granule neurons and analyze dendritic spine density using ImageJ.
Perform statistical analysis of test results using appropriate ANOVA or t-tests and plot graphs with GraphPad Prism software.

steps: 1. Grow and maintain worms on NGM plates seeded with Escherichia coli (OP50) at 20°C.
2. Use specific worm strains for experiments as detailed in the protocol.
3. Cross worm strains as necessary to create specific genetic backgrounds for the experiments.
4. To induce de-silencing of silenced strains, grow them for 1–2 generations at 25°C and then for a generation at 20°C before analysis.
5. Create GFP::rad-51 strains using CRISPR-Cas9 with pDD282 and assess functionality.
6. Generate spo-11 mutations using CRISPR-Cas9 and assess loss of function via DAPI body counts.
7. Image live worms using MetaMorph software with a 100×/1.4 NA oil Leica microscope, setting light intensity to 5% and exposure times to 500 ms for GFP and 20 ms for D&C.
8. Determine row position in the PMT by counting from the distal tip and identify transition zones (TZ) and pachytene stages.
9. Perform time series projects of microirradiated live worms using Metamorph Multidimensional Acquisition every 2 minutes, imaging a 9 μm range at 1 μm intervals for 46 time points.
10. Process imaged stacks from live imaging in MetaMorph to create maximum projections for each time point.
11. Score nuclei for foci using FIJI-Image J and record the size of foci, noting any abnormally large foci as focus clusters.
12. Assume worm death during live imaging when foci stop moving and other signs of life cease, and stop scoring nuclei at this point.
13. Image fixed slides using the DeltaVision wide-field fluorescence microscope system and deconvolve images with softWoRx software.
14. Record length of gonad and location of foci using cell width counts from the distal tip cell.
15. Microirradiate target nuclei in the germline using an Andor micropoint 365nm pulsed laser, attenuating the output as specified.
16. Recover microirradiated worms immediately after the procedure and dissect at appropriate time intervals.
17. Prepare live image slides with worms on 3% agarose pads or in live imaging petri dishes, using M9, Polybead polystyrene beads, and coverslips.
18. Recover worms from live imaging setups by submerging slides in M9 or lifting agarose pads in petri dishes and using a glass pipet.
19. Place recovered worms on NGM plates seeded with OP50 until time of dissection.
20. Dissect worms to extract gonads, fix, and stain with specific antibodies and DAPI for immunofluorescent staining.
21. Measure distances between foci within a mid-pachytene nucleus using FIJI-ImageJ straight line measurement tool.
22. Analyze fixed samples, defining RAD-51 formed large foci as clusters and not counting small foci as positive in microirradiation experiments.
23. Perform RNA interference by growing RNAi cultures, placing bleached embryos on OP50 NGM plates, and transferring to RNAi plates before microirradiation.
24. Conduct statistical analysis using Kruskal-Wallis test and Mann–Whitney U test as appropriate.
25. Perform apoptosis assays by imaging the bend region of gonadal arms post-microirradiation and counting CED-1::GFP engulfed nuclei.
26. Conduct COSA-1 assays by targeting all TZ nuclei with irradiation, recovering worms, and counting GFP::COSA-1 foci in dissected late pachytene region nuclei.
1. Obtain 12 male 3-month old BALB/cARC mice and 12 male 3-month old C57BL/6JARC mice from the Animal Resources Centre (Murdoch, WA, Australia).
2. House mice in groups of four in individually ventilated caging with bedding, on a 12-h light cycle (lights on at 0700), in a room maintained at 21 ± 1°C and 50 ± 10% humidity.
3. Use individual tail markings to identify animals throughout the experiment.
4. Restrict food to 90% of the mice's free-feeding body weight by adjusting the amount of food provided daily, ensuring all mice can consume the food without fighting.
5. Provide food at the same time each day with ad libitum access to water in the home cage.
6. Acclimate mice to a liquid reward by providing a small quantity of strawberry milk in a 50 ml falcon tube lid in their home cage for 3 days prior to training.
7. Habituate mice to the testing room by bringing their home cage into the room for a minimum of 30 min prior to each session.
8. Train mice on the Habituation stage to collect a reward when the tray illuminates, requiring completion of 50 trials within 20 min on two consecutive sessions.

9. Progress mice to Initial Touch, teaching them to touch a white square on the screen to receive a 3× reward or a single reward after 30 s of no activity, completing 100 trials within 30 min or a maximum of five sessions.
10. Move mice to Must Touch Stimuli, requiring them to touch the stimuli to receive a reward and complete 100 trials in under 30 min.
11. Advance mice to Must Initiate, where they must enter the reward tray to start the trial and complete 100 trials in 60 min.
12. Finally, progress mice to Punish Incorrect, where a time-out occurs if they touch the incorrect location, requiring them to complete 100 trials in under 60 min with at least 70% correct.

13. After completing training, move mice to the Visual Discrimination (VD) task, where they must discriminate between two visual stimuli to receive a reward, completing 100 trials in under 60 min and achieving at least 80% correct.

14. Once the VD task is acquired, switch the contingency for reversal so the previously unrewarded stimulus must now be selected, conducting testing until reaching the criteria of 80% correct or a maximum of 20 sessions.
15. Place mice individually in square Perspex chambers to measure locomotor activity, tracking body position with an array of infrared beams over a 30 min session.
16. Individually place mice into a clear cylindrical vessel containing 25°C water for the Forced Swim Test (FST), recording activity with an overhead video camera for 10 min.
17. Allow mice to dry in a cage filled with paper towel prior to returning to their home cage after the FST.
18. Analyze behavioral test videos using tracking software to measure total distance traveled and total duration of immobility.
19. Clean the touchscreen apparatus, open field chamber, and FST vessel with 70% ethanol between animals.

20. Analyze results using SPSS software, applying independent t-tests, ANOVA, or repeated measures ANOVA with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons and Greenhouse-Geisser correction for violation of sphericity.

steps.description: Maintain DT40, Non-KI(B), KI(B), and KI(MΦ) cell lines as previously described.
Subject Non-KI(B), KI(B), and KI(MΦ) (2 x 10^7 each) to the iChIP procedure as previously described.
Subject DT40 cells to the in vitro enChIP procedure as previously described.
Use the complex of CRISPR RNA (crRNA) targeting the Pax5 promoter and trans-activating crRNA (tracrRNA) as Pax5 gRNA for in vitro enChIP.
Fragment chromatin DNA to an average length of about 2 kbp.
Isolate the target region by iChIP or in vitro enChIP.
Purify the DNA after isolation.
Prepare DNA libraries using TruSeq ChIP Sample Prep Kit, selectively concentrating DNA fragments around 0.4 kbp in length.
Subject the libraries to DNA sequencing using the HiSeq platform according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Perform NGS and data analysis as previously described.
Map NGS data onto the reference genome galGal4 using ELAND.
Detect narrow peaks of each iChIP-Seq dataset using Model-based Analysis of ChIP-Seq 2 (MACS2) with default parameters.
Generate images of NGS peaks using Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV).
Obtain Cas9 expression plasmid and chimeric single guide RNA (sgRNA) expression plasmid from Addgene.

Clone double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) encoding the target sequences downstream of the U6 promoter in the sgRNA expression plasmid or synthesize and clone DNA fragments coding the U6 promoter, target sequence, gRNA scaffold, and termination signal in plasmids.

Transfect DT40 cells (1 x 10^7) with Cas9 expression plasmid (120 µg), sgRNA expression plasmids (120 µg) targeting each end of a target genomic region, and pEGFP-N3 (0.3 µg, Clontech) by electroporation using Gene Pulser II at 250 V and 950 µF.
One day post-transfection, sort GFP-positive cells and expand them individually.
Extract genomic DNA from expanded cells and perform genotyping PCR to confirm targeted locus deletion.
Perform PCR cycles: heating at 94°C for 2 min followed by 30 cycles of 98°C for 10 s, 60°C for 30 s, and 68°C for 1 min.
Extract total RNA and perform quantitative RT-PCR as previously described.
Perform ChIP assays with DT40 cells (2 x 10^6) using antibodies against H3K4me1, H3K27ac, and histone H3 as previously described.
Purify DNA using ChIP DNA Clean & Concentrator and use as template for real-time PCR with SYBR Select Master Mix on Applied Biosystems 7900HT Fast Real-Time PCR System.

steps.1: Obtain C57BL/6 mice (8 weeks old, 18–22 g) from Jackson Laboratories.

steps.2: House mice in groups under controlled conditions at 25°C with a 12:12-h light–dark cycle.

steps.3: Provide unrestricted access to standard mouse chow and tap water.

steps.4: Dilute DSS (40,000 Da, 3% wt/vol) to a 3% solution in drinking water.

steps.5: Administer the DSS solution to the mice for 7 days.

steps.6: Sacrifice the mice by CO2 euthanasia after the treatment period.

steps.7: Collect a 50 mg sample of the proximal colon from each mouse for RNA extraction.

steps.8: Isolate total RNA from the colonic tissues using TRIzol reagent according to the manufacturer's instructions.

steps.9: If indicated, purify RNA via precipitation with lithium chloride.

steps.10: Assess RNA integrity by 2% agarose gel electrophoresis.

steps.11: Incubate RNA with 0.1 volume of 8 M LiCl diluted in RNase-free water on ice for 2 hours.

steps.12: Centrifuge the mixture at 14,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C and discard the supernatant.

steps.13: Dissolve the RNA pellet in 200 μl of RNase-free water.

steps.14: Repeat the incubation with LiCl, centrifugation, and pellet dissolution steps once more.

steps.15: Precipitate the RNA at -20°C for 30 minutes using 0.1 volume of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) and 2 volumes of 100% absolute ethanol.

steps.16: Centrifuge the RNA at 14,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C and discard the supernatant.

steps.17: Wash the RNA pellet with 100 μl of 70% ethanol and centrifuge at 14,000 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.

steps.18: Remove the supernatant and dissolve the RNA in 20–50 μl of RNase-free water.

steps.19: Synthesize cDNA using the Maxima First-Strand cDNA Synthesis Kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.

steps.20: Quantify expression of the total RNA by qPCR using Maxima SYBR Green/ROX qPCR Master Mix in a Realplex Thermal Cycler with primer sequences for 36B4.

steps.21: Measure polymerase enzymatic activity using the EvaEZ™ Fluorometric Polymerase Activity Assay kit with recombinant Taq DNA polymerase incubated with water or DSS.

steps.22: Quantify enzymatic activity by fluorescence using the Realplex Thermal Cycler, reading the fluorescence every 1 minute for 60 minutes at 72°C.

steps.23: Measure reverse transcriptase enzymatic activity using the EnzChek Reverse Transcriptase Assay kit with M-MuLV RT incubated at 25°C with water or DSS.

steps.24: Quantify enzymatic activity by fluorescence using a Synergy 2 Multi-Mode Microplate Reader.

steps.25: Perform SPR experiments using gold sensor chips and the BI-2000 SPR machine.

steps.26: Activate each gold biosensor chip covered with carboxydextran using EDC/NHS.

steps.27: Inject purified M-MuLV Reverse Transcriptase onto the chip.

steps.28: Pass RNA, previously primed using random primers and incubated at 42°C, or primed RNA incubated with DSS in different concentrations over the chip twice.

steps.29: Obtain a two-step interaction curve and use the laser deviation angle as the parameter for binding affinity.

steps.30: Perform statistical analysis of the data using an unpaired two-tailed t-test with GraphPad Prism 5 software, considering p <0.05 as statistically significant.

steps.description: Obtain plasma cells from the synovial fluid of a patient with anti-CCP–positive RA.
Isolate antibody-secreting cells from synovial fluid mononuclear cells using the fluorescent foci method.
Sort single citrulline-specific B cells by flow cytometry from the peripheral blood of RA patients using an antigen-tetramer system.
Perform peptide ELISAs to assess binding to citrulline-containing and arginine-containing peptides.
Add monoclonal antibodies to the wells of the ELISA plate at a concentration of 5 μg/ml, diluting by a factor of 2 down to 0.15 ng/ml.
Analyze all reactive samples in at least 3 independent experiments.
Dilute full-length proteins (fibrinogen, recombinant vimentin, and histone H4) in PBS and coat on Nunc Maxisorp 96-well plates.
Block plates with 5% milk powder in PBS.
Incubate plates for 3 hours at 37°C with citrullination buffer or buffer control.
Incubate with ACPAs at a concentration of 5 μg/ml, diluted by a factor of 2 down to 0.15 ng/ml.
Carry out sequential incubation with secondary Fc-specific, HRP-conjugated anti-human IgG or biotin-conjugated human IgG1-Fc plus HRP-conjugated streptavidin.
Develop with SeramunBlau fast TMB and read results with Spectra Fluor.
Synthesize peptides covering all arginine and lysine sites of extracellular matrix proteins and RA-related proteins.
Dilute monoclonal antibodies to a concentration of 1 μg/ml and synovial fluid and serum samples to a dilution of 1/100.
Scan for citrulline and homocitrulline reactivity with each monoclonal antibody using a NimbleGen MS200 Scanner.
Calculate median fluorescence intensities based on a peptide signal intensity variation of 25 pixels.
Determine the cutoff value for positive signals as 5 times the fluorescence intensity of the 98th percentile of values for a set of non-ACPA monoclonal antibodies.
Solubilize full-length proteins in 8M urea at 1 mg/ml for Western blot analyses.
Electrophorese proteins on 12.5% SDS-PAGE gels and blot to a nitrocellulose membrane.
Incubate blots overnight at 37°C in citrullination buffer with hPAD2 or with buffer control.
Incubate with ACPAs at 5 μg/ml and sequentially with the same secondary antibody used for the full-length protein ELISA.
Visualize results using Amersham Hyperfilm.
Analyze the 4 flanking amino acids from each posttranslational residue using the WebLogo application to generate consensus sequences.
Perform statistical analysis using Mann-Whitney nonparametric test and one-way Kruskal-Wallis test followed by Dunn's test for multiple comparisons.
Consider P values less than or equal to 0.05 as significant and use GraphPad Prism for calculations and visualizations.
Culture cells in DMEM + 10% fetal bovine serum (S+ medium) at 37°C and 5% CO2 or in different serum-free formulations as detailed in SI Materials and Methods.
Add recombinant ribonuclease inhibitor (RI; NEB) at a final concentration of 4–8 U/ml, either at the time of medium renewal or following collection of cell-conditioned media.
Centrifuge the cell-conditioned medium at 2000 × g to remove cells and debris.
Further centrifuge the cell-conditioned medium for 2.5 h at 100,000 × g and 4°C in a Beckman Coulter Optima XPN-90 ultracentrifuge using a SW40 Ti rotor to remove vesicles.
Concentrate the supernatant to approximately 250 μl using 10,000 MWCO ultrafiltration units (Vivaspin 20, Sartorious Stedim Biotech).
Subject the concentrated supernatant to size-exclusion chromatography or RNA extraction with TRIzol as per the manufacturer's instructions.
Concentrate the 100,000 × g supernatants of the cell-conditioned medium by ultrafiltration with successive dilutions using PBS to remove phenol red and small molecules.

Inject 500 μl of concentrated EV-depleted fractions into a Superdex S200 10/300 column (Amersham, GE) and perform size exclusion chromatography (SEC) at 0.9 ml/min in 0.22 μm-filtered 1× PBS with an Äkta Pure (GE healthcare) FPLC system.
Centrifuge all samples at 16,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C before injection into the columns.

Collect fractions of 0.25 ml while monitoring the absorbance at 260 and 280 nm. Deconvolute chromatograms in silico using empirically determined 260/280 ratios from pure bovine serum albumin (BSA) and synthetic tRNAGlyGCC 5′ halves (of 30 nt).
Purify RNA from selected chromatographic peaks using TRIzol LS according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Dilute the obtained RNA in 8 μl of ultra-pure RNase-free water, and use 7 μl as input for NGS library preparation using the NEBNext Small RNA Library Prep Set for Illumina (New England Biolabs).
Perform sequencing in a MiSeq benchtop sequencer for 200 cycles. Analyze as detailed in SI Materials and Methods.

Perform Northern blots using 10% denaturing gels transferred to positively-charged nylon membranes with digoxigenin-labeled DNA probes and an alkaline phosphatase-labeled anti-digoxigenin antibody (Roche).
Visualize signals with CDP-Star ready-to-use (Roche) and detect using ChemiDoc imaging system (BioRad).
Prepare adherent mouse bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDC) as described in referenced material.
Add selected chromatographic fractions or synthetic RNAs to 1 × 10^6 BMDCs.
At t = 24 hours, harvest cells and analyze by flow cytometry using a CyAn ADP Analyzer (Dako).

steps: 1. Compare the morphology and expression levels of co-stimulatory molecules and MHC class II antigens between iPS-DCregs and BM-DCregs.
2. Assess the antigen uptake ability of iPS-DCregs under IFN-γ stimulation using fluorescein isothiocyanate uptake tests with ovalbumin (OVA) and dextran.
3. Measure mRNA expression levels of suppressive cytokines (TGF-β1, Arg-1, PD-L1, HO-1) in iPS-DCregs and compare them to BM-DCcons.
4. Set up an allogeneic mixed lymphocyte reaction (MLR) using naive T cells from CBA mice and stimulate them with B6 BM-DCcons to induce alloreactive proliferation.
5. Add B6 BM-DCregs and iPS-DCregs to the allogeneic MLR system and measure the proliferative response of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells.
6. Establish OVA-specific MLR by co-culturing T cells from B6-background TCR transgenic mice OT-II (CD4+) and OT-I (CD8+) with OVA-pulsed B6 BM-DCcons at a 20:1 ratio for 3 days.
7. Add B6 BM-DCregs and iPS-DCregs to the OVA-specific MLR and assess the proliferative response.
8. Perform in vivo regulatory function assessment using a proliferation lymph node assay (PLNA) by adoptively transferring OT-II or OT-I T cells into wild-type B6 mice.
9. Inject OVA-pulsed B6 BM-DCcons combined with iPS-DCregs or controls subcutaneously into the recipients' footpads and analyze T cell proliferation from the PLNs.
10. Immunize CBA mice with B6-derived DCs and isolate their spleens 7 days after immunization.
11. Assess spleen cells (SPCs) by flow cytometry (FCM) and set up for secondary immunization in vitro.
12. Elute T cells from SPCs using a nylon column and co-culture them with B6 BM-DCcons or BALB/c BM-DCcons for MLR as secondary immunization.
13. Analyze the proliferation of CD8+ and CD4+ FOXP3- effector T cells after 3 days of co-culture.
14. Inject different types of DCregs intravenously into CBA recipients prior to receiving a B6 heart allograft and monitor allograft survival.
15. Compare the median survival time (MST) of allografts among groups treated with different DCregs and controls.
16. Perform histological analysis of lymphocyte infiltration in allografts postoperatively.
17. Assess the infiltration of CD8+ BrdU+ T cells in allografts and splenocytes from recipients.
18. Measure mRNA expression levels of Perforin/Granzyme B and proinflammatory cytokines in allografts.
19. Analyze the increase of Tregs in allografts using immunohistochemistry and FCM.
20. Detect the expression of Tregs activity markers CTLA-4 and GITR in allografts.
21. Deplete Tregs using anti-CD25 monoclonal antibody (mAb) in recipients treated with iPS-DCregs and observe the effect on allograft acceptance.
22. Perform adoptive transfer of splenocytes from long-term surviving recipients into naive CBA mice and assess allograft acceptance.
23. Block TGF-β1 using anti-TGF-β1 mAb in recipients treated with iPS-DCregs before and after transplantation and evaluate allograft acceptance.
24. Harvest SPCs for FCM analysis to determine the effect of TGF-β1 blockage on Tregs proportion and character induced by iPS-DCregs immunization.
25. Analyze the expression of FOXP3, Ki-67, CCR4, and CCR7 in CD4+ CD25+ cells and calculate their percentage in the total spleen.
Obtain rooted petunia plantlets (Petunia x hybrida L. lines P720, W115 [cv. MD], Blue Spark, and Blue Ray) from Danziger–Dan Flower Farm (Mishmar Hashiva, Israel).
Grow plants in a greenhouse under a 25/20°C day/night temperature regime and a 12/12 h light/dark photoperiod, with the light period starting at 0800 h.
For dynamic headspace analysis, collect petunia P720 flowers at different developmental stages at 1600 h.
For diel floral emission analysis, collect petunia P720 flowers at anthesis stage and initiate headspace collection at 0300 h with 4-h intervals for 24 h.

Collect volatiles emitted from detached flowers (three flowers per sample) using an adsorbent trap consisting of a glass tube containing 200 mg Porapak Type Q polymer held in place with steel mesh plugs.
Elute trapped volatiles using 1.5 ml hexane and add 2 μg isobutylbenzene to each sample as an internal standard.
Generate a calibration plot with increasing isobutylbenzene concentrations to determine the relative amounts of target volatiles within each sample.

To determine free volatile compounds (aglycones) in the corolla limbs, collect petal tissues (150 mg fresh weight from at least three different flowers), grind in liquid nitrogen, and extract in 800 μl hexane containing 2 μg isobutylbenzene as the internal standard.
Incubate extracts with shaking at 150 rpm for 2 h, centrifuge (10,000 g for 10 min), and further centrifuge and evaporate the supernatant prior to chromatography.

To extract glycosylated scent compounds, grind corolla limb tissue (150 mg fresh weight from at least three different flowers) in liquid nitrogen, suspend in 1.2 ml 80% MeOH:DDW (v/v), and sonicate for 20 min.
Centrifuge samples (16,000 g, 10 min), vacuum-dry the supernatant, and resuspend in 0.9 ml 0.2 M citrate–phosphate buffer, pH 5.4.
Add Viscozyme (150 μl) to hydrolyze and release sugar-bound aroma compounds and incubate overnight at 37°C with the enzyme.
Extract samples in 800 μl hexane containing 2 μg isobutylbenzene as the internal standard and prepare for GC–MS analysis as described for aglycone determination.
Calibrate the protocol for glycoside extractions by extending the evaporation of the samples while heating to promote emission of volatiles.
Perform GC–MS analysis using a TRACE GC 2000 equipped with an Rtx-5SIL mass spectrometer fused-silica capillary column and a TRACE DSQ quadruple mass spectrometer.
Use helium as the carrier gas at a flow rate of 1 ml/min, set injector temperature to 220°C (splitless mode), interface to 240°C, and ion source to 200°C.
Perform the analysis under a temperature program with 2 min of isothermal heating at 40°C, followed by a 7°C/min oven temperature ramp to 250°C, then 2 min of isothermal heating.
Equilibrate the system for 1 min at 70°C before injection of the next sample.
Record mass spectra at 3.15 scan/s with a scanning range of 40–450 mass-to-charge ratio and electron energy of 70 eV.
Identify compounds based on NIST/EPA/NIH Mass Spectral Library data and comparison of mass spectra and retention times with those of authentic standards.
Collect petunia flowers (line P720) 1 DPA at 1500 h for 2H5-phe-feeding experiments.
Excise detached corollas 1.5 cm below the limbs and place in a 150-μl solution containing 30 mM 2H5-Phe stable isotope.
Incubate for 20 min, wash corollas twice with DDW, and then transfer to water for the rest of the experiment.
Collect limb samples (150 mg) at different time points (0.5, 2, 4, 6, and 9 h after transfer to water) to determine the internal pool of glycosylated scent compounds.
Detect conjugated compounds derived from labeled and non-labeled 2H5-Phe as described by Boatright et al. (2004).
Perform transient overexpression of pBINPLUS carrying CaMV 35S-driven AnBGL1 in petunia line P720 flowers.

Subject petunia buds 1 day before anthesis to vacuum infiltration with a mix of Agrobacterium tumefaciens strain AGLO carrying pRCS2-35S:GFP and bacteria carrying pBINPLUS-35S:AnBGL1vac or pBINPLUS-35S:AnBGL1cyt in a 1:1 (v/v) mixture.
Use AGLO carrying only pRCS2-35S:GFP as a control.
Examine open flowers three days postinfiltration using a fluorescence binocular microscope under white and UV light with GFP filters.
Excise GFP-positive tissues and extract and analyze glycosylated scent compounds by GC–MS.
For β-glucosidase activity assay, grind tissues (300 mg) in liquid nitrogen and extract in 1.2 ml 50 mM phosphate buffer pH 4.3, containing 10 mM EDTA and 4 mM dithiothreitol.
Measure total protein level using the Bradford method.
Quantify enzyme activity using pNPG as the substrate and calculate as the amount of liberated p-nitrophenyl per mg protein per 1 min of reaction time.
Isolate protoplasts from petunia petals (line Blue Ray) and assay viability with fluorescein diacetate solution.
Image fluorescent cells using a fully motorized epifluorescence inverted microscope with a GFP filter.
Isolate intact vacuoles from protoplasts using a Ficoll step gradient and centrifuge for 45 min at 1,500 g.
Evaluate vacuole purity using light microscopy and western blot analysis.
Measure anthocyanin content of protoplasts and vacuoles as described by Spitzer-Rimon et al. (2010).
Extract glycosides from protoplasts and vacuoles and quantitate by GC–MS.
Extract proteins for western blot analysis by precipitating aliquots of protoplasts and vacuoles in trichloroacetic acid, washing with acetone, and resuspending in extraction buffer.
Treat extracts with Tris-saturated phenol, wash with MeOH–ammonium sulfate, and then with 80% acetone.
Resuspend pellets in NuPAGE LDS Sample Buffer and incubate for 5 min at 55°C prior to electrophoresis.
Analyze samples on NuPAGE 4–12% Bis–Tris gels and transfer to iBlot nitrocellulose membranes for western blot analyses.
Block membranes with skimmed milk-based solution, react overnight at 18°C with primary antibodies, wash, and incubate with secondary antibody.
Develop membranes with SuperSignal West Pico Chemiluminescent Substrate and autoradiography using Image Quant Las 500.
Calculate significance of differences between treatments using Student's t-test (P ≤ 0.05) with SigmaPlot software v13.0.

1. Synthesize TO1 PEG4 desthiobiotin (TO1-Dtb) and TO3 PEG4 desthiobiotin (TO3-Dtb) using TO1-acetate and TO3-acetate, respectively, with EZ link amine PEG4 desthiobiotin as precursors following the established protocol.
2. Confirm product identity by electrospray ionization–mass spectrometry in the positive mode.
3. Wash streptavidin agarose beads twice with Buffer A and three times with Buffer B.
4. Add TO1-Dtb to the washed beads and incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
5. Wash the beads once with Buffer B to remove any unbound dye.
6. Prepare the yeast U1M strain and confirm the presence of the U1-Mango gene and the absence of the WT allele by PCR and DNA sequencing.
7. Create a double-tagged strain containing both U1M and a SNAP-tagged Snp1 protein by homologous recombination.
8. Confirm transformants by PCR and by labeling of Snp1-SNAPf with fluorescent SNAP ligands.
9. Prepare yeast whole-cell extracts using the liquid N2 method and a ball mill.
10. Label yeast whole-cell extracts with SNAP-Surface 549 tag and incubate with Murine RNase inhibitor, Protease Inhibitors, DTT in Buffer B at room temperature for 30 minutes.
11. Add yeast whole-cell extracts to TO1-Dtb saturated agarose beads and incubate at 4°C for 1 hour in a rotator.
12. Wash the beads twice with Buffer B at 4°C and once more at 30°C.
13. Elute the snRNP with Buffer B supplemented with biotin at 37°C for 30 minutes.
14. Concentrate a portion of the biotin eluate and load onto an SDS PAGE gel for visualization.
15. Extract the remaining biotin eluate with phenol, chloroform, and ethanol precipitate using glycogen.
16. Resuspend the pellet in water and analyze by RT-primer extension assay.
17. Perform RNA analysis by RT-primer extension and solution hybridization using labeled primers and Maxima Reverse Transcriptase.
18. Construct the p6SRDM_T7 plasmid with point mutations and clone it into the pEcoli-Cterm-6xHN plasmid.
19. Express the 6SRDM RNA in E. coli BL21 (DE3) cells and prepare the extract.
20. Purify 6SRDM associated RNPs by mixing E. coli native extract with TO1-Dtb derivatized agarose beads and eluting with WB containing free biotin.
21. Fractionate the 6SRDM RNP complex by size-exclusion chromatography and measure TO1-Dtb fluorescence.
22. Analyze 6SRDM RNP complexes and commercial RNAP by LC–MS/MS at the University of British Columbia Proteomics Core Facility.
23. Partially purify eGFP-HE from E. coli strain RL1314 using a modified Burgess and Jendrisak protocol.
24. Perform two-color gel-imaging analysis of the Mango and eGFP-tagged 6S:RNAP complex.
25. Obtain the two-photon spectrum of 6SM:TO3-Dtb by measuring fluorescence intensity over a range of two-photon excitation wavelengths.
26. Perform fluorescence cross-correlation spectroscopy by adding increasing amounts of RNAP-eGFP extract to a fixed amount of 6SM and TO3-Dtb.

steps.action: Extract viral RNA from 140 μl of virus culture supernatants or patients’ plasma using the QIAamp Viral Min Kit.
Elute RNA in 50 μl of nuclease-free water.
Store the eluted RNA at -80°C until use.
Construct mutant viral RNA templates using a fast mutagenesis system based on the 3′-UTR region of the DENV-4 genome.
Obtain the 3′-UTR fragment of DENV-4 using StarScript II Probe One-Step qRT-PCR Kit with primers F3/134 and B3/4.
Sub-clone the 3′-UTR fragment into pMD18-T plasmid vector.
Fuse a T7 promoter to the 5′-end of the primer F3/134.
Construct various mutants using site-directed mutagenesis with mutagenic primers and confirm by Sanger sequencing.
Obtain mutant RNAs through in vitro transcription with T7 RNA polymerase.
Quantify mutant RNAs using spectrophotometric absorbance at 260 nm.
Calculate copy number of each mutant RNA using the provided formula.
Prepare a 25 μl reaction mix of the novel RT-LAMP assay with the specified components.
Add 3 μl of RNA to the RT-LAMP assays.
Perform the RT-LAMP reaction at 63°C for 60 min with 0.4 μM SYTO 9 as fluorescent dye for real-time monitoring.
Use the Light Cycler 96 real-time PCR System for monitoring the RT-LAMP reaction.
Determine the sensitivity of the novel DENV RT-LAMP assay using ten-fold serial dilution of RNA from four DENV stocks.
Perform RT-qPCR assay to determine the RNA copy numbers of the virus stocks.
Obtain a standard curve by 10-fold serial dilutions of in vitro transcribed DENV RNA standard.
Determine the LOD of the novel DENV RT-LAMP assay using 10-fold and fivefold serial dilutions of RNA from each virus stock.
Perform Probit regression analysis to determine the LOD.
Evaluate the performance of the novel RT-LAMP assay using 153 plasma samples from dengue-suspected patients.
Perform NS1 antigen detection using One-Step Dengue NS1 RapiDip InstaTest kit.
Perform specific RT-PCR assays using PrimeScript One Step RT-PCR Kit Ver.2.
Subject positive samples by RT-PCR assay to Sanger sequencing and phylogenetic analysis.
Test the RNA stocks again using both the novel and the conventional RT-LAMP assays.
Calculate the concordance rate of the four methods.
Perform further RT-nested PCR amplifications on samples with discrepancies between RT-PCR and RT-LAMP assays.
Process amplicons for Sanger sequencing and further sequence analyses.
Add 120 μM hydroxynaphthol blue to the RT-LAMP reaction mix for visual detection.
Perform another visual RT-LAMP assay with WarmStart Colorimetric LAMP 2X Master Mix.
Observe color change at 30, 40, 50, and 60 minutes during the visual RT-LAMP assay.
Ensure all dengue-suspected patients have provided written informed consent.

steps.description: Grow Escherichia coli NEB5α and BL21(DE3) in LB broth with aeration at 250 rpm.
Transform plasmids into E. coli cells by electroporation.
Select transformants by plating on LB agar with the appropriate antibiotic and incubate at 37°C overnight.
Grow M. smegmatis MC2 155 in the conditions described below.
Use EZ-Vision DNA dye to visualize DNA and CloneAmp HiFi PCR Premix to amplify DNA.
Insert M. smegmatis DnaBi1 in-frame into kanR of pUC4K using Gibson assembly.
Prepare plasmids using an E.Z.N.A. plasmid minikit.
Verify all clones by sequencing.
Screen KD fusions in E. coli on LB media containing carbenicillin and various amounts of kanamycin to identify candidates that require splicing for survival.
Report the degree of survivability as CFU per kanamycin concentration.
Use the 3D structure of KanR to analyze the context and properties of the +1 serine residues.
Calculate rSASA, distance to the dimer interface, and distance to the active site for each serine residue using PyMOL.
Grow M. smegmatis MC2 155 in standard 7H9 (liquid) and 7H10 (solid) media.
Subclone KD154 into a mycobacterial shuttle vector, pMBC283, using Gibson assembly.
Prepare 7H10 media without albumin or catalase for spot titer studies.
Perform two-fold dilutions of cells starting from OD600 values of 3 to 5 and spot on 7H10 media.
Spot 1.25 μl of cells at each titer and grow at 30°C for 5 days.
Express MIG using BL21(DE3) and induce with 0.5 mM isopropyl β-D-1-thiogalactopyranoside at 30°C.
Lyse cells in MIG buffer using a tip sonicator and pellet the samples.
Incubate the soluble lysate at 16°C for ∼16 h for M. smegmatis DnaBi1 and ∼24 h for M. leprae DnaB.
Add zinc acetate at indicated concentrations prior to incubation.
Treat samples with a 2× excess of EDTA after 1-h incubation with zinc to verify reversibility of splicing inhibition.
Separate samples on 8% to 16% Tris-glycine gels and detect GFP-containing products.
Use ImageJ for quantitation and GraphPad Prism for analysis.
Purify M. smegmatis DnaBi1 using a chitin affinity column followed by gel filtration chromatography.
Concentrate M. smegmatis DnaBi1 to 13 mg/ml.
Grow M. smegmatis DnaBi1-zinc crystals using a hanging-drop vapor diffusion method.
Transfer crystals to a cryoprotectant solution and flash-cool in liquid nitrogen.
Collect diffraction data at 100 K and process images.
Solve the crystal structure by molecular replacement and refine using Phenix.
Deposit the final refinement of the M. smegmatis DnaBi1-zinc structure in the Worldwide Protein Data Bank under PDB ID: 6OWN.

steps.action: Purify polyclonal ACPA IgGs and non-ACPA control IgGs from pooled and non-pooled sera of RA patients.
Purify polyclonal antiproteinase 3 (PR3) IgGs and non-anti-PR3 control IgGs from sera of a patient with PR3-associated vasculitis.
Isolate monoclonal antibodies from patients with RA and express recombinantly as IgG1.
Perform extensive quality control testing on all IgG including specificity evaluation, size exclusion chromatography, aggregation test and LAL endotoxin test.
Generate F(ab’)2 antibody fragments and purchase RF IgM antibody.
Obtain synovial biopsies from healthy volunteers and RA patients with informed consent.
Assess fibroblast migration using IncuCyte Zoom live cell imaging system or scratch assay.
Perform adhesion assays using 16-well E-plates and xCELLigence System Real-Time Cell Analyzer.
Wash cells with phosphate buffered saline and starve for 2 hours in serum-free medium when indicated.
Add citrullinated or native human purified fibrinogen, recombinant vimentin, α-enolase and histone H4 as pretreatment to ACPA and control IgGs at 4°C overnight.
Inhibit PI3K with wortmanin and PTEN with SF-1670.
Inhibit PAD activity with Cl-amidine or GSK199 for 72 hours prior to scratching.
Inhibit histone acetyltransferase or deacetylase enzymes with anacardic acid or trichostatin A, respectively.
Culture fibroblasts in the presence or absence of IL-8 or TNF-α.
Analyse cytokine levels using Cytometric Bead Array and measure matrix metalloproteinases by ELISA.
Stain FLS with primary antibodies followed by HRP-conjugated antibodies and develop with Vectastain Elite ABC and DAB, then counterstain with Mayer’s haematoxylin.
For confocal microscopy, incubate cells and tissues with primary and secondary antibodies and counterstain with 4,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole.
Analyse starved and non-starved FLS whole cell lysate by mass spectrometry for detection of citrullination.
Load cell lysates on an SDS-PAGE gel, transfer to nitrocellulose membranes and incubate with primary and peroxidase-conjugated secondary antibodies.
Collect cells using non-enzymatic detachment reagent, stain with fluorochrome-labelled antibodies and analyse by FACSVerse flow cytometer.
Analyse data using Kurskal-Wallis test followed by Dunn’s multiple comparison test or two-way analysis of variance, followed by Tukey’s post hoc test using GraphPad Prism 6 software.

steps: 1. Perform peptidomics analysis of soybean (Glycine max) xylem exudate to identify root-to-shoot long-distance mobile peptides.
2. Focus on homologs in Arabidopsis CLEs and compare the amino acid sequence of the XAP4/GmCLE32 peptide with Arabidopsis CLE1–7.
3. Collect Arabidopsis xylem exudate and perform nano-liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (nano-LC–MS/MS) analysis to detect the presence of mature CLE2 peptide.
4. Treat plants with the photosynthesis inhibitor 3-(3,4-dichlorophenyl)-1,1-dimethylurea (DCMU) or prolonged darkness to examine CLE2 response to low-carbon conditions.
5. Measure CLE2 mRNA levels in roots after DCMU and dark treatments and observe the effects of sucrose application on CLE2 upregulation.
6. Examine the expression of CLE1 and CLE3–7 under low-carbon conditions.
7. Measure sugar (sucrose and glucose) and starch contents in the roots and leaves of plants sampled at the end of the day in the absence of stress.
8. Generate cle2cle3 double mutant and cle1-7 septuple mutant using CRISPR/Cas9 technology.
9. Compare sucrose and glucose levels in roots of cle2cle3 and cle1-7 mutants with wild-type (WT) plants.
10. Conduct a gain-of-function analysis of CLE2 using the Commelina Yellow Mottle Virus (CoYMV) promoter in transgenic lines.
11. Measure mRNA level of CLE2 in transgenic lines and compare with WT line.
12. Measure sucrose contents in roots and mature leaves of prCoYMV:CLE2 and prCoYMV:CLE3 lines.
13. Apply synthetic mature CLE2 peptide to the rosette leaves of WT plants and measure starch and sugar contents in shoots and roots after 24 hours.
14. Apply CLE2 peptide to the cle1-7 septuple mutant and measure sucrose contents to assess restoration.
15. Evaluate shoot and root mass in the cle1-7 mutant under normal light conditions and on sucrose-free media.
16. Apply sucrose to the media to observe its effect on the shoot/root mass ratio in the cle1-7 mutant.
17. Examine the growth of cle mutants under diurnally fluctuating light conditions.
18. Perform quantitative expression analysis of genes involved in sucrose transport, synthesis, and degradation in leaves and roots of prCoYMV:CLE2 and prCoYMV:CLE3 lines.
19. Analyze the mRNA levels of sucrose-related factors in cle1-7 leaves and compare with cle2, cle3, and cle2cle3 mutants.
20. Apply CLE2 peptide to cle1-7 leaves and measure SUC2 mRNA levels for potential rescue.
21. Analyze the mRNA levels of sucrose degradation enzymes in roots of cle1-7 and other mutants.
22. Perform grafting experiments to combine roots and shoots of WT and cle1-7 plants and measure SUC2 expression levels in grafted plants.

steps.action: Prepare cortical and hippocampal neuron cultures from mouse embryos (E15.5; strain C57BL/6J).
Collect tissue specimen in Dissection media (HBSS 1×, 6 mM MgSO4, 10 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 10 μg/ml gentamicin).
Cultivate tissue in Neuronal complete medium (Neurobasal 1×, B27 supplement 1×, 0.5 mM L-glutamine, 10 μg/ml gentamicin).
Plate high-density neuronal cultures (750–1000 cells/mm2) on 12 mm diameter coverslips in 24-well plastic tissue culture plates.
Transduce primary neuronal cultures at DIV4 with GFP-expressing pLVTH virus at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 2.
Treat neurons with 10 ng/ml FGFb and 5 ng/ml EGF for 10 minutes.
Seed cortical cultures in a 96-well plate at a concentration of 5 × 103 cells/cm2 and incubate at 37°C for 24 hours for MTT assay.
Add MTT solubilized at 5 mg/ml in PBS 1× to a final concentration of 0.25 mg/ml in medium and incubate for 2 hours at 37°C.
Decant the medium and solubilize formazan precipitates in 200 μL of DMSO.
Measure the absorbance at 570 nm using a spectrophotometer.
Wash neurons in PBS and lyse in RIPA buffer.
Clarify lysate by centrifugation for 20 minutes at 16,000 g at 4°C.
Measure protein samples via standard Bradford assay.
Dilute a proper volume of sample containing an equal amount of proteins with 0.25% 5× Laemmli buffer and load onto 10% SDS-PAGE gels.
Transfer proteins onto nitrocellulose membrane at 80 V for 120 minutes at 4°C.
Apply primary antibodies overnight in blocking buffer.
Detect proteins using the ECL prime detection system and acquire images with ChemiDoc Touch imaging system.
Perform protein quantification by measuring the optical density of the specific bands with ImageLab software.
Infect neuronal cultures with viruses at DIV 1–2 for immunofluorescence.
Characterize mitochondrial superoxide content at DIV14 by incubating with 2.5 μM Mitosox Red for 45 minutes at 37°C.
Fix neurons in 4% paraformaldehyde and 4% sucrose at room temperature.
Randomly choose GFP positive neurons for quantification.
Acquire fluorescence images using a LSM Zeiss 510 confocal microscope with appropriate objectives.
Automatically trace and quantify neurites using NeuronStudio software.
Log and analyze data in Microsoft Excel.
Immunostain neurons for MAP2, synapsin1–3, and PSD95 at DIV14.
Acquire images using a Leica SP8-X confocal microscope at 63× resolution.
Mask MAP2-positive dendrites using ImageJ and quantify synapsin- and PSD95-positive clusters using Cell Profiler.
Perform whole-cell recordings in voltage- and current-clamp modes in a temperature-controlled recording chamber.
Use pClamp 10.0 software and Digidata 1550 interface for data acquisition.
Fabricate patch electrodes from thick borosilicate glass capillaries using a Sutter P-1000 puller.
Perfuse cells with Krebs solution.
Perform voltage-clamp recordings of evoked ionic currents and acquire spontaneous synaptic activity in gap-free mode.
Record mEPSCs in the presence of 200 nM TTX and analyze using Clampfit 10.0 Program.
Carry out current-clamp recordings of spontaneous and evoked firing activity.
Compute parameters of APs using Clampfit 10.0 Program.
Automatically calculate passive properties of the cells by Clampex.
Monitor series resistance during the experiments and discard recordings with changes over 20% of its starting value.
Express all data as mean ± SEM and log into GraphPad Prism.
Analyze data with an unpaired Student’s T-test or ANOVA followed by Tukey’s post hoc test.
